items.title: hrx: Bind sub-buffers at their byte offset.
items.body:
## Motivation

A caller can build a buffer that is a region of one it already owns: the same device allocation, a shorter length, and a byte offset into the parent. Prefill uses that to point at one range of a weight or hidden-state buffer without allocating a second copy.

The HRX shim dropped the offset. `run::add_binding` recorded `(handle, 0, size)`, and flush and invalidate used the same zero. The device therefore read and wrote the start of the parent allocation. A view of bytes 4096 through 8192 was submitted as bytes 0 through 4096.

## Technical Details

The slice now keeps that byte offset on the buffer. Dispatch, flush, and invalidate pass it through to `hrx_buffer_flush_range` and `hrx_buffer_invalidate_range`. The slice does not own the allocation, so releasing it does not free the parent. `get_handle().get()` returns the parent handle, which is how callers tell several slices of one allocation apart. An unmapped parent stays unmapped.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

items.title: fix(hrx): shut down the device without touching destroyed statics
items.body:
Follow-up to #787. ~Runtime() entered the executable-cache and coherence-map function-local statics after they had already been destroyed.

Release this instance's stream. The instance whose hrx_gpu_initialize() succeeded then calls hrx_gpu_shutdown(), which destroys the device and its heap. A module that saw HRX_STATUS_ALREADY_EXISTS releases only its own stream.

items.title: ci: add ASR test workflow for Whisper transcription
items.body:
## Summary

Adds an **ASR Test** workflow that measures speech recognition on real NPU hardware whenever ASR-related code changes. It also gives PRs #510, #794 and #798 a way to be validated on hardware. CI currently has no hardware coverage for ASR, because the model sweep's audio task is disabled.

**What it measures** (`.github/script/asr_test.py`):
- **Accuracy:** WER, or CER for ja and zh, on 84 FLEURS files with human transcripts. Each set and the pooled total are reported, with each file's errors capped at its reference length so that one runaway transcript can't swamp a set.
- **Runaways:** transcripts longer than 1.5× the reference, which is what a decoder stuck in a repetition loop produces.
- **Speed:** seconds of processing per second of audio.
- **Formats:** `json`, no `response_format`, and `verbose_json` must agree.
- **Chat transcription:** WER of `gemma4-it:e2b` (whose audio front end E4B and the flash variants share) and `gemma4-it:12b` (which has its own, `modeling_gemma4_12b_audio.cpp`).

**Feature groups.** These only fail the run when required; otherwise they are reported as warnings:

| Group | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `verbose_json` | Segments are ordered, inside the clip, non-empty, and join into the text; `duration` equals the clip length |
| `timestamp_rules` | Segments never overlap; the first starts within 1 s |
| `window_tail` | No phrases repeated across 30 s windows |
| `language` | Forcing the language doesn't hurt accuracy; it is reported back; unknown codes are rejected |
| `prompt` | A prompt doesn't hurt accuracy, and names in it are spelled as given |
| `quiet_log` | No transcripts in the server log |

Only `prompt` is required by default, because it is the only group `main` passes on every platform. `main`'s Linux HRX build loops on the long-form file, so it fails `window_tail`; a PR that adds repeats is still caught by the baseline comparison. A PR that makes `main` pass another group adds it to `ASR_REQUIRE` in the workflow.

**Comparison.** On a pull request, `main`'s latest build runs first on the same runner and becomes the baseline. The run fails if:
- the pooled error rate rises by more than 1 point;
- any set rises by more than 5 points (sets have 10 files, so one flipped decode moves them a point or more);
- or the number of runaways grows.

The report also shows how many files changed and the drift from `main`'s transcripts. Pushes to `main` and the weekly run compare against `asr_eval/expected.json` instead, with 2 points of slack on the pooled rate (versus 1 point against `main`) and the same 5 points per set. Its rates are kept per platform, because identical sources decode differently on each: `main` scores 18.55% pooled on Linux, 22.63% on Linux HRX, 18.61% on Windows and 19.44% on Windows HRX, and some sets differ by up to 5 points. A manual dispatch can test any PR's builds (`pr`) and set `require` and `max_drift`.

**Evaluation set** (`.github/script/assets/asr_eval/`, 6.8 MB, CC BY 4.0, attributed in its README):

| Set | Files | Audio |
|---|---|---|
| `en-short` | 20 | single window |
| `en-long` | 3 | ~83 s each, two window boundaries |
| `en-longform` | 1 | 308 s |
| `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `zh`, `ar` | 10 each | |

`build_asr_eval.py` rebuilds the set deterministically from the FLEURS Parquet files.

**Triggers:** pull requests and pushes to `main` that touch any of the following, plus a weekly run and manual dispatch:
- the Whisper engine, its NPU kernels and prebuilt libraries;
- FFmpeg, FFT (`fftw`, `pocketfft`) and `audio_process_utils`;
- the chat-model audio front ends;
- `rest_handler.cpp`, `server.cpp` and `multipart.*`;
- the test's own files.

Linux and Windows are both tested, default and HRX builds alike.

**Report.** A `summary` job writes one report to the run's summary page. It starts with a verdict per model and platform. Then each model gets its own section with Linux, Linux HRX, Windows and Windows HRX side by side:
- `whisper-v3:turbo`: accuracy per set against `main`; runaways, changed files and speed; checks by group; failures and warnings per platform.
- each chat model: WER against `main`, plus its own failures.

Each job's own report, results JSON and raw responses are in its artifact. The script also refuses to start if its port is already taken, so it can't end up testing another server by mistake.

## Validation of #510, #794 and #798 on hardware

I ran each PR's CI-built Linux portable against `main` (`77bc6bdd`) on a Strix NPU. Each run required the default groups plus the ones that PR adds.

| | `main` | #510 | #794 | #798 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pooled error rate | 18.55% | 18.55% | **7.14%** | 18.82% (+0.27) |
| en-short / en-long / longform WER | 9.71 / 11.89 / 16.53 | same | **4.74 / 4.87 / 6.48** | 9.71 / 11.89 / 15.24 |
| de / es / fr WER | 38.1 / 15.4 / 27.7 | same | **7.0 / 2.9 / 7.0** | 38.6 / 15.4 / 29.3 |
| ja / zh CER, ar WER | 19.4 / 13.5 / 41.7 | same | **6.8 / 12.4 / 17.7** | 20.0 / 15.4 / 42.8 |
| Runaways | 3 | 3 | **0** | 3 |
| Files changed vs `main` | – | 0 | 50/84 | 18/84 |
| Gemma chat WER | 5.05% | 5.05% | 5.05% | 5.05% |
| Result | pass | **fail**: `verbose_json` | **fail**: `prompt` | pass |

**#510 (`verbose_json`).** On `main`'s decoder, segments are invalid in 28 of 84 files, 5 of them English short clips:
- they end past the clip (for example 0.00–24.74 s on an 8.6 s clip) in 24 files;
- they are zero-length or empty in 8 files;
- they go backwards in 4 files.

Most of this comes from `main`'s decoder, which #794 fixes. #510 could still clamp segment ends to the duration and drop empty segments.

**#794 (decode loop).** It reproduces the claimed gains on every set, removes all runaway loops, rejects unknown language codes, and stops logging transcripts. However, `prompt` looks broken. When a prompt word is spoken in the clip, the transcript drops everything up to it:
- `prompt="China's"` returns " economic output." instead of the whole sentence;
- the WER of the prompted clips goes from 6.1% to 41.5%.

When the prompt words aren't spoken before the end, it works as intended: "Fichte" is then spelled correctly. The timestamp rules can't be observed without `verbose_json` (#510).

**#798 (pocketfft).** No regression: pooled +0.27 points, no new runaways, and Gemma is unchanged. 18 files changed, nearly all by one word or character; one change is a fix (漏れ効いた → 漏れ聞いた). That's the expected effect of slightly different FFT rounding tipping a borderline greedy decode. `en-short` is byte-identical.

## Test plan

- [x] `main` and the three PR builds run through `asr_test.py` on a Strix NPU (results above)
- [x] Chat transcription is repeatable at temperature 0 (two runs byte-identical)
- [x] Baseline lookup tested against a fake `gh`: pull request with an expired `main` run and a missing HRX baseline, dispatch with a PR number, and push without a baseline
- [x] `actionlint` is clean apart from the custom runner labels
- [x] Windows and Windows HRX jobs on CI (run 38853168399): `main` then this PR's build, about 18 min per job; 42/42 checks pass, 0 files changed (this PR changes no engine code)
- [x] `main`'s Linux HRX build measured locally for `expected.json`: it loops on the long-form file ("the state of the state of …"), 36.8% WER against 16.5% on Linux
- [x] Linux and Linux HRX jobs on CI (run 38865384844): 42/42 and 41/41 checks pass, matching the local runs
- [x] Combined report rendered from the four CI results, plus a failing example (#794's `prompt` checks)
- [ ] `gemma4-it:12b`: first tested by this PR's next CI run. It could not run locally, because the test NPU was busy with another CI job.

items.title: fix: replace FFTW with pocketfft and ship third-party notices
items.body:
## What

**FFT replacement**
- Vendors [pocketfft](https://github.com/mreineck/pocketfft) (BSD-3-Clause, header-only, the FFT behind numpy and scipy) from the `cpp` branch at `c90e55b`.
- `src/include/audio_process_utils/rfft.hpp` is the only file that includes pocketfft, which keeps its config macros consistent across translation units. It provides `audioproc::rfft_many()`, a batched r2c function with interleaved `(re, im)` output in the same layout as FFTW.
- Ports the three call sites:
  - `audioproc.cpp`
  - `audioprocAVX512.cpp` (one batched call replaces `fftwf_plan_many_dft_r2c`)
  - the Whisper `FFT400` class.
- Note: pocketfft's odd-size DCT-IV code is derived from FFTW and is used under BSD-3 *with permission of Frigo & Johnson* (stated in the header). FLM doesn't call it.

**FFTW removal**
- CMake: removes FFTW discovery on vcpkg and pkg-config, removes it from all link lists, and drops the portable Linux step that bundled `libfftw3*.so`.
- Packaging: removes FFTW from the Inno and WiX installers, `debian/control`, the `Dockerfile` and the portable CI summary.
- Test builds: removes FFTW from the `src/test/*` CMake and Makefile harnesses.
- Deletes `src/lib/libfftw3*-3.{dll,lib,def,exp}` and `src/include/fftw3.h`.
- I checked the prebuilt engine libraries: no `src/lib/{xrt,hrx}` DLL or `.so` imports FFTW.

**Third-party notices**
- Adds `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` at the repo root. It is installed by `cmake --install` (covering the .deb and portable tarball), staged by both `get_files.bat` scripts, and included in the Inno `[Files]` section and a WiX component.
- Covers FFmpeg (LGPL-2.1+, confirmed from the license strings in every shipped DLL), curl, zlib, Abseil, protobuf, Boost.Program_options, XRT, aiebu, tokenizers-cpp, HF tokenizers, SentencePiece and its bundled darts-clone and esaxx, msgpack-c, Oniguruma, pocketfft, nlohmann/json, minja, base64, biovault_bfloat16, Unicode data and the MSVC runtime.
- Also lists all 75 Rust crates resolved by `cargo tree` for the tokenizers FFI on both the Windows and Linux targets, with their licenses and copyright lines; all are permissive.
- License texts are copied verbatim from upstream (version-pinned where applicable).
- The Linux portable tarballs and Windows portable zips are built from explicit file lists, which had left out `LICENSE_RUNTIME.txt` and `LICENSE_BINARY.txt` as well. This PR adds both, plus `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`, to every portable packaging step.

## Verification
- **Numerical:** compared against a locally built FFTW 3.3.10 and a double-precision direct DFT.
  - Covered every changed path: `rfft_batch`, `rfft_magnitude_batch`, `stft_power_batch`, their AVX512 variants, and `FFT400` compiled from the header.
  - Covered sizes 400 (Whisper), 512 and 1024, the odd size 401, and zero-padded frames.
  - Maximum relative error against FFTW is ≤ 4e-7 (float rounding). pocketfft and FFTW are equally accurate against the f64 DFT.
- **Performance:** for 3000×400 frames (one 30 s Whisper window), the batched pocketfft call takes about 1.6–2 ms versus about 5 ms for FFTW `plan_many`. Per-frame calls take about 3–4 ms versus about 2 ms for FFTW. Both are negligible next to NPU inference.
- **Compile:** the changed sources compile with no warnings under GCC 13 and Clang 18 (`-Wall -Wextra`).
- **Not built locally:** the full `flm` build, on Windows and on Linux with XRT/FFmpeg. **This PR's CI covers those (Windows build, debian, portable).**

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- The portable Linux build **links FFmpeg statically** into `flm`. Under LGPL that means users must be able to relink against their own FFmpeg (e.g. by providing object files). Linking FFmpeg dynamically and bundling its `.so` files would be simpler.
- HRX portable packages bundle host runtime libraries resolved at build time (`libgomp`, `libmvec`, …), and these aren't listed in the notices yet.
- Legal/OSPO should review the FFmpeg source-availability wording in the notices.

items.title: fix(validate): run NPU stack check before opening the device
items.body:
## Problem

`flm validate` fails on v1.0.8 on a working NPU system (it passed on v1.0.7):

```
[Linux]  Kernel: 7.0.0-31-generic
[ERROR]  No NPU device found.
[Linux]  Memlock Limit: 3710 MB
[Linux]  NPU platform: aie2p
```

Since #748 (commit 1313ef8e, "feat(phi4): run Phi-4-mini-instruct Q8_0 GGUF through ryzenai-corelib"), `main()` opens the shared NPU device (`open_npu_device()`) before dispatching commands. `sanity_check_npu_stack()` then opens `/dev/accel/accelN` itself, and amdxdna refuses a second open of the same device from one process with `EBUSY`. The probe loop skipped any open error other than `ENOENT` silently, so no device was found.

strace of v1.0.8 `flm validate`:

```
openat("/dev/accel/accel0", O_RDWR) = 3          <- open_npu_device()
openat("/dev/accel/accel0", O_RDWR) = -1 EBUSY   <- sanity_check_npu_stack()
openat("/dev/accel/accel1", O_RDWR) = -1 ENOENT
```

## Fix

- On the non-RAI path, handle `validate` before `open_npu_device()`. The RAI path is unchanged: its validate does not probe the device and relies on the corelib status printed earlier in `main()`.
- In the probe loop, report `EBUSY` (human-readable error plus a `"busy": true` device entry in `--json`) instead of skipping it silently, so this kind of regression points at its cause.

## Testing

On Linux 7.0.0-31, amdxdna 0.15, NPU FW 1.1.2.64 (aie2p, 8 columns), using the patched binary in the v1.0.8 portable tree:
- `flm validate` finds `/dev/accel/accel0` and exits 0
- `flm validate --json` reports `"amd_device_found": true`, `"ready": true`

items.title: feat(hrx): add hrx::Runtime::shutdown()
items.body:
Refs #792 (part 2).

Since #787 and #800, `~Runtime()` releases the stream and, in the owning instance, calls `hrx_gpu_shutdown()`, at exit only. An embedder that unloads Whisper on idle keeps the accel fd and 64 MiB of device memory until it exits.

- `shutdown()` refuses while an executable with `refs > 0` or any buffer is alive. It frees `refs == 0` executables (`build_or_get_executable()` path), then runs the same release as `~Runtime()`: own stream, and `hrx_gpu_shutdown()` only in the owner, which resets `runtime_owns_shutdown()`.
- Idempotent. The next `rt()` initializes again. `~Runtime()` after `shutdown()` does nothing.
- Several `Runtime` instances (Windows, one per DLL): the fd only closes once every instance has called `shutdown()`. Not tested on Windows.

Nothing in `flm` calls `shutdown()` yet.

## Validation

Krackan (Ryzen AI 7 350), NPU fw 1.1.2.64, Ubuntu 26.10, kernel 7.3, HRX 2026.10.13. The #792 repro with `-DFLM_HAS_RUNTIME_SHUTDOWN`, 3 cycles of create, load, encode, destroy, `shutdown()`, plain and ASan+UBSan:

| point | drm-total-memory | accel fds |
|---|---|---|
| after first encode | 725,120 KiB | 1 |
| all FLM objects destroyed | 65,580 KiB | 1 |
| after `shutdown()` | 0 | 0 |
| next cycle, after first encode | 725,120 KiB | 1 |

Exit without `shutdown()`: `~Runtime()` releases, ASan clean. `flm serve`: one transcription, then SIGTERM, unchanged. Two instances emulated on Linux (`-fno-gnu-unique`): see the comment on this PR. Not run: Windows, the XRT build.

items.title: fix(whisper): make the ASR decode loop behave like Whisper
items.body:
Fixes #793.

Six commits, one per defect. Each builds on its own.

1. `fix(whisper): stop forcing a timestamp every 16 text tokens` - the forced timestamp ends segments early and the model then emits EOT. Main cause of the WER gap.
2. `fix(whisper): feed the language token to the decoder` - the prompt becomes `<|startoftranscript|><|lang|><|task|>`. The empty translate branch now feeds `<|translate|>`.
3. `feat(server): honour language and prompt in /v1/audio/transcriptions` - `language` (ISO 639-1) replaces detection; an unknown code is an error. `prompt` goes behind `<|startofprev|>` as openai-whisper does (leading space, text tokens only, last 223 tokens). Both optional.
4. `fix(whisper): apply Whisper's timestamp rules, <|30.00|> included` - 1501 timestamps built from an integer index; first timestamp at most `<|1.00|>`; after a closing timestamp only a timestamp or EOT; no empty segments; timestamps never go back.
5. `fix(whisper): do not decode the tail of a full window twice` - text after the last timestamp of a full 30 s window is held and dropped, since the next window starts there. `last_time_stamp` is reset per window.
6. `fix(server): do not log transcripts by default` - "Audio content: ..." is printed only with `FLM_LOG_RAW_OUTPUT` set.

`Whisper::generate` gains two defaulted parameters (`language`, `prompt`), so `flm run` and `test/whisper_npu` are unchanged.

## Validation

Built with `cmake --preset linux-default -DFLM_USE_HRX=ON` against HRX 2026.10.13, g++ 15.3, Ubuntu 26.10, Krackan (Ryzen AI 7 350), NPU fw 1.1.2.64, model Whisper-V3-Turbo-NPU2 @ 594eecd2. Each commit was built and run through `flm serve`, one POST per clip. WER %, CER for ja/zh.

| after commit | en 82 (<= 30 s) | en ~80 s x10 | long-form 302 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 7.23 | 12.46 | 1.29 |
| 1 forced timestamp | 3.14 | 2.98 | 1.29 |
| 2 language fed (auto) | 3.14 | - | - |
| 3 `language` set | 3.09 | 3.09 | 1.29 |
| 4 timestamp rules | 3.14 | 3.09 | 1.29 |
| 5 window tail | 3.14 | 3.04 | 1.29 |
| 6 logging | 3.14 (auto: 3.14) | 3.09 | 1.29 |

FLEURS, 10 clips per language:

| | de | es | fr | ja | zh | ar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 30.3 | 30.6 | 40.8 | 34.4 | 32.7 | 66.1 |
| commit 1 | 3.2 | 2.6 | 13.7 | 10.0 | 15.4 | 23.9 |
| commit 2, auto language | 3.2 | 2.6 | 13.0 | 8.9 | 28.0 | 20.4 |
| commit 6, `language` set | 3.2 | 2.6 | 13.7 | 10.0 | 15.4 | 23.5 |

- Commit 2 alone makes zh worse: one clip is detected as English, and once the decoder is told so it writes English. Before, the detection was thrown away. Setting `language` (commit 3) fixes it, which is the point of honouring the field.
- `prompt` works: on the 302 s clip, `prompt="Gryce Challoner Sweetwater"` spells both names right (0 -> 2 "Gryce", 0 -> 1 "Challoner"), WER 1.29 -> 1.00.
- Differences of 0.05 between rows are encoder nondeterminism (1-2 clips change case or punctuation between passes), not the patches.
- Commit 4 without its rules (only the 1501-entry map) took the ~80 s set to 21.2%: a window closed on `<|30.00|>`, greedy decoding ran on past it into a repetition loop, and the next window opened seconds late. That variant is not in this PR.
- Commit 5 changes nothing measurable on these sets once commit 1 is in: windows end on a closing timestamp almost always. It stops the duplication by construction.
- With commit 6, the serve log of a 296-request run has no transcript text.
- CPU reference, faster-whisper large-v3-turbo greedy on the same clips: 2.41% English.

Not run: the Windows build, the XRT build, `flm run` with audio, the CI deb matrix. Compiles clean with the HRX preset on Linux.

items.title: Whisper decode loop truncates sentences, ignores language and prompt, logs transcripts
items.body:
`flm serve --asr 1` loses about half its accuracy in the host-side decode loop, not on the NPU. Same NPU, same libs, same weights: English WER goes from 7.2% to 3.1% with the fixes below. Non-English is worse today (FLEURS de 30%, fr 41%, ar 66%) and comes back to 2-23%.

Five defects, all in `src/common/whisper/modeling_whisper.cpp` and `src/server/`:

1. Forced timestamp every 16 tokens. `Whisper::generate` (L185-224 at 419cf1b) forces the next token into the timestamp range after 16 text tokens. The model takes it as the end of the segment and often emits EOT. Sentences stop mid-word: "...has count <|26.20|>", "...von Sch", "...l'USOC, Com".
2. Language token never fed. The language is sampled from the `<|startoftranscript|>` logits (L149) but not fed back. The decoder sees `<|startoftranscript|><|transcribe|>`, a prompt Whisper was not trained on.
3. `language` and `prompt` ignored. `/v1/audio/transcriptions` reads only `model` and `file` (server.cpp L978-982). OpenAI clients that set `language` or `prompt` get neither, with no error.
4. `<|30.00|>` is not a timestamp. `_build_time_map` sums `0.02f` while `<= 30.00`. Float error stops it at 29.98, so the map has 1500 entries, not 1501. There are also no timestamp rules: text can follow a closing timestamp, and a window can open at any time, not only within the first second.
5. Audio over 30 s: the text after the last timestamp of a window is emitted, then the next window starts at that timestamp and decodes it again.

Also: every transcript is printed to stdout ("Audio content: ..."). Under systemd that is the journal. For dictation that is a privacy problem.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 26.10, kernel 7.3.0-6-generic, amdxdna 0.10 (in-tree)
- Framework 13, AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 (Krackan, XDNA2, 1022:17f0 rev 20), NPU firmware 1.1.2.64
- FastFlowLM main 419cf1b (1.0.8 + HRX 2026.10.13), built from source with `cmake --preset linux-default -DFLM_USE_HRX=ON`, g++ 15.3. Same behaviour in the 1.0.8 release tarball.
- Model FastFlowLM/Whisper-V3-Turbo-NPU2 @ 594eecd2, xclbins from `src/xclbins/Whisper-V3-Turbo-NPU2`
- `flm validate`: fw_ok, enough_cols, kernel_ok true; memlock_ok false (8 MiB). serve works at 8 MiB with HRX 2026.10.13 anyway.

## Repro

```
FLM_MODEL_PATH=<dir with models/Whisper-V3-Turbo-NPU2> flm serve --asr 1 --port 52625
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F model=whisper-v3:turbo -F file=@clip.wav -F language=de
```

Any 10-30 s English clip with a sentence over ~16 tokens shows (1). A German or Chinese clip with `language` set shows (2) and (3). An 80 s clip shows (5) when the model leaves text after the last timestamp of a window.

## Evidence

82 English clips <= 30 s (LibriSpeech plus noisy variants), 10 clips of ~80 s made by concatenating them, 60 FLEURS clips (10 each of de, es, fr, ja, zh, ar). Each clip is one POST to `flm serve`. WER with Whisper-style normalisation; CER for ja and zh. Expected: close to faster-whisper large-v3-turbo greedy on CPU on the same clips, 2.41% English.

| build | en 82 | en ~80 s x10 | FLEURS de / es / fr / ja / zh / ar |
|---|---|---|---|
| main 419cf1b | 7.23 | 12.46 | 30.3 / 30.6 / 40.8 / 34.4 / 32.7 / 66.1 |
| + fixes, `language` set | 3.14 | 3.04 | 3.2 / 2.6 / 13.7 / 10.0 / 15.4 / 23.5 |

English errors S/D/I go from 49/82/7 to 43/13/4: the loss is truncation. Removing the forced timestamp alone gives 3.14. I reproduced the loop in Python against the same `libwhisper_npu.so` and got the same numbers (8.01% vs 2.98% on the 1.0.8 libs), so the NPU math is fine.

## Fixes

I have fixes ready on a branch, one commit per defect, and will open a PR: `fix(whisper): stop forcing a timestamp every 16 text tokens`, `feed the language token to the decoder`, `feat(server): honour language and prompt`, `apply Whisper's timestamp rules, <|30.00|> included`, `do not decode the tail of a full window twice`, `fix(server): do not log transcripts by default` (only with `FLM_LOG_RAW_OUTPUT`).

One thing I tried and dropped: making `<|30.00|>` a timestamp without the timestamp rules. It took the ~80 s set from 3.1% to 21.2%: a window ended on `<|30.00|>`, greedy decoding carried on past it into a repetition loop, and the next window skipped its first seconds. The rules fix both.

Not addressed: no temperature fallback, no compression-ratio or no-speech gates, greedy only. The encoder output is also not deterministic run to run (1-2 of 82 clips change punctuation or case between passes), which is NPU-side.

items.title: libwhisper_npu leaks 1.33 MB per encode_audio; NPU memory is only returned by a full HRX shutdown
items.body:
Two problems for anyone who keeps Whisper loaded, or unloads it on idle, in a long-running process.

## 1. Host leak in `WhisperEncoder::add_bias_optimized`

Every `whisper_npu::encode_audio` leaks 1,331,200 bytes. It is linear, never freed, and survives `~whisper_npu` and `hrx_gpu_shutdown`. `flm serve` grows by about 1.3 MB per 30 s window: ~160 MB per hour of speech. Our `flm serve` was at 1.03 GB RSS after 296 requests (1.0.8 started at 264 MB).

Where: `libwhisper_npu.so` (`src/lib/hrx`, main 419cf1b), `WhisperEncoder::add_bias_optimized(buffer<bf16>&, buffer<bf16>&, buffer<bf16>&) [clone .isra.0]` at +0x28670. It calls `operator new[](n_out * 4)` at +0x286e0, converts the bf16 bias to float into it, uses it, and returns at +0x28952 without `operator delete[]`. The pointer never leaves the frame. Same code in the 1.0.8 tarball (+0x286d0).

Per encode: 32 layers x (one 20,480 B block, the fc1 bias, plus four 5,120 B blocks: q, v, out_proj, fc2 biases) plus four 5,120 B blocks outside the loop = 1,331,200 B.

heaptrack (10 vs 40 encodes, diffed): 1.331 MB per encode, 100% from `add_bias_optimized` via `WhisperEncoder::forward` -> `whisper_npu::Impl::encode_audio`. Decode steps and `clear_context` leak nothing.

Suggested fix: free the scratch (or use a `std::vector`), or convert the biases to float once in `load_weights`. The source is not public, so this needs the maintainers.

## 2. Device memory after destroy

With HRX 2026.10.13 (main), destroying every FLM object returns most NPU memory: 725 MiB -> 64 MiB (`drm-total-memory` in fdinfo). jtuyls/hrx f4151e05f ("drop model contexts and buffers on unload") fixed the 582 MiB BO cache that 1.0.8 kept.

What is left: 64 MiB and the `/dev/accel` fd stay until the process exits. The only public way to get them back is to tear the runtime down by hand:

```
hrx_stream_release(hrx::Runtime::get().stream);  // the stream holds a device ref
hrx_gpu_shutdown();
rt.stream = nullptr; rt.dev = nullptr; rt.ok = false;  // poke the singleton's fields
```

That works (fd closed, 0 KiB, re-create works, 3/3 cycles here and 20/20 on 1.0.8). But it writes `hrx::Runtime` fields from outside, and the order is a trap: `hrx_gpu_shutdown()` with the stream still alive returns OK, keeps the old device, and the next init stacks a second one (1.26 GB after two cycles on 1.0.8).

Ask: a supported `hrx::Runtime::shutdown()` in `hrx_cpp.hpp`. I have a small patch for it and will open a PR.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 26.10, kernel 7.3.0-6-generic, amdxdna 0.10 (in-tree), RLIMIT_MEMLOCK 8 MiB
- Framework 13, AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 (Krackan, XDNA2, 1022:17f0 rev 20), NPU firmware 1.1.2.64
- FastFlowLM main 419cf1b, `src/lib/hrx` engine libs, HRX `flm-hrx-amdxdna-v2026.10.13` (jtuyls/hrx e53f299). Also seen with the 1.0.8 tarball (HRX c023c3e).
- Model FastFlowLM/Whisper-V3-Turbo-NPU2 @ 594eecd2

## Repro

Standalone, about 150 lines, in https://gist.github.com/quine00/393fe0c1d38550bcb5d4ee8988b864f5 (`whisper_npu_leak.cpp`, `build.sh`). It creates the engine the way `Whisper::load_model` does, runs N encodes on a synthetic mel, destroys everything, then tears HRX down, and prints VmRSS, malloc in use (`mallinfo2`) and the accel fd's `drm-total-memory` at each step.

```
FLM=<FastFlowLM checkout> HRX=<hrx-amdxdna-2026.10.13 package dir> ./build.sh
./whisper_npu_leak <.../Whisper-V3-Turbo-NPU2> <FastFlowLM>/src 20 3
```

Output, cycle 0 (cycles 1 and 2 identical apart from the growing leak):

```
start                  VmRSS=  5708 kB  malloc_in_use=    74960 B  accel_fds=0 drm-total-memory=0 KiB
loaded                 VmRSS=199384 kB  malloc_in_use=196672256 B  accel_fds=1 drm-total-memory=707 KiB
after 1 encode         VmRSS=212784 kB  malloc_in_use=210298832 B  accel_fds=1 drm-total-memory=725120 KiB
after more encodes     VmRSS=238868 kB  malloc_in_use=237010496 B  accel_fds=1 drm-total-memory=725120 KiB
malloc in use grew 1335583 B per encode_audio over 20 calls
all FLM objects gone   VmRSS= 36056 kB  malloc_in_use= 29099008 B  accel_fds=1 drm-total-memory=65580 KiB
after runtime teardown VmRSS= 36032 kB  malloc_in_use= 28908864 B  accel_fds=0 drm-total-memory=0 KiB
```

Expected: malloc in use back near the start value after destroy, and a supported call that gets `drm-total-memory` to 0.
Actual: 29 MB (21 encodes x 1.33 MB) stays allocated forever; 64 MiB and the fd stay until a hand-rolled teardown. After three cycles, 85 MB is leaked.

No memlock preload or raised limit was needed: HRX 2026.10.13 runs at 8 MiB.

items.title: Make the test harnesses link again: backend registry and engine lib path
items.body:
## Summary

Most standalone test harnesses under `src/test/` no longer link on main. This fixes the two causes that apply to all of them.

- **Backend registry.** `automodel.cpp` builds engines through the backend registry, so a harness that compiles it also has to compile `model_backend.cpp` and define `register_builtin_backends`, as `create_new_model.md` says. Only the MiniCPM-V and rai harnesses did. The other 20 now do. Each registers the families of the engine libraries it already links, taken from `builtin_backends.cpp`. For example, `qwen3_npu` registers `qwen3`, `qwen3-it`, `qwen3-tk` and `deepseek-r1-0528`. Qwen3.5-Omni builds its engine itself, so its harness registers nothing.
- **Engine library path.** Since the HRX split, the prebuilt engine libraries live in `src/lib/xrt` and `src/lib/hrx`, but `add_npu_test` still linked from `src/lib`. It now links from `src/lib/xrt`, since the harness CMake is XRT-only.

Also:
- Whisper's Makefile drops `automodel.cpp`. Whisper never used it, and its CMake build already did without it.
- The MiniCPM-V harness CMake gets the image sources, AVX-512 and ffmpeg setup that its Makefile already has, the same as the other vision harnesses.

## Testing

Windows, MSVC, CMake path:

- Results:
  - MiniCPM-V, gemma_npu, gemma_text_npu, gpt_oss_npu, hunyuan_npu, lfm2_npu, llama_npu, nanbeige_npu, phi4_npu, qwen2_npu, qwen2vl_npu, qwen3_5vl_npu, qwen3_6_moe_npu, qwen3_npu, qwen3vl_flash and qwen3vl_npu build and link.
  - gemma4_12b, gemma4e_flash, gemma4e_npu, qwen3_5_omni_npu, qwen3_8mtp_npu and whisper_npu still fail to link, for the reasons under "Not in this PR". None of them has registry errors left.
- The MiniCPM-V harness runs all four turns on the NPU: a prompt, a prompt-cache follow-up, a thinking prompt and an image.
- The Linux Makefiles are not tested.

## Not in this PR

- `gemma4_12b` and `qwen3_5_omni_npu` CMake don't link `swresample` or `fftw`, which their audio sources need.
- `qwen3_8mtp_npu` CMake is missing its image sources.
- `gemma4e_*` and `whisper_npu` link `libfftw3-3.lib`, which `src/lib` ships only as a `.def` and `.dll`.

#790 adds the chat library to the same harnesses. The two PRs merge without conflicts in either order.

items.title: Shared chat parsing and constrained decoding for the OpenAI endpoints
items.body:
## Summary

Every model carried its own reasoning and tool-call parser, and `tool_choice` was a single masked token. This replaces both with one shared chat library (`src/common/chat`) and adds constrained decoding to `/v1/chat/completions`.

**Parsing**
- The chat format is detected once per model from its chat template and vocabulary: `hermes_json`, `qwen_xml`, `gemma4`, `lfm2_pythonic`, `harmony` or `content_only`. The server log prints the result at load (`Chat format: ...`).
- Streamed and non-streamed replies go through the same parser, so the streamed deltas (`reasoning_content`, `content`, `tool_calls`) add up to the non-streamed message. Tool markup only counts as a call when the request has `tools`.
- The per-model `parse_stream_content` / `parse_nstream_content` overrides, the parser state on `AutoModel` and `openai_policy.hpp` are removed (about 4,300 lines).
- Gemma4 now stops at `<|tool_response>` and GPT-OSS at `<|call|>`.

**Constrained decoding** (new dependency: xgrammar v0.2.8, Apache-2.0, as a submodule)
- `tool_choice` (`auto`, `none`, `required`, a named function), `parallel_tool_calls` and `response_format` (`json_object`, `json_schema`) become a per-token constraint. Malformed values, unknown functions, `required` without tools and unbuildable schemas return 400.
- Every model samples through `AutoModel::_sample`. Models that force think-prefix tokens in `generate()` report them with `_force_token` / `_skip_insert_sample`.
- When a model's thinking is off, the grammar does not offer a reasoning block either. Before this, Gemma4 could escape into a thought block under `response_format` and answer with empty content.
- Qwen3.8-MTP turns speculative decoding off under a constraint.

**Behaviour change: streaming usage**
- Following OpenAI, a streamed response carries `usage` only when the request sets `stream_options.include_usage`. Every chunk then has `usage: null` except a final chunk with no choices. Clients that read usage from streams without asking for it will no longer get it.

**Since the last sync with main**
- MiniCPM-V 4.7 (added on main) moves onto the shared library. Its template is detected as `qwen_xml` with reasoning.
- The test harnesses that compile `automodel.cpp` now get the chat sources and xgrammar. The xgrammar build moves into `common/chat/chat_sources.cmake`, shared by `flm`, `add_npu_test` and the rai frontend tests.

The raw text models write to the stream is unchanged, so the CLI, `/v1/completions` and the Ollama endpoints behave as before. `docs/docs/instructions/server/openapi.md` documents the new request fields.

## Testing

- `flm` builds in Release (MSVC, XRT).
- MiniCPM-V 4.7 on `flm serve`, 18 end-to-end checks on `/v1/chat/completions`, with thinking on and off: plain chat (stream and non-stream, no raw tags in output), tools with `tool_choice` auto, none, required and a named function, `response_format` `json_schema`, and image input. All pass.
- The MiniCPM-V harness runs all four turns, including a prompt-cache follow-up and an image.
- `test_gemma4_frontend` (rai) builds and passes.

## Not in this PR

- Test harnesses still fail to link on main for reasons unrelated to this branch: they don't compile `model_backend.cpp` or register a backend, and the Windows CMake path links engine libraries from `src/lib` instead of `src/lib/xrt`. #791 fixes these.
- Until that PR lands, whisper's Linux Makefile compiles `automodel.cpp` without the chat sources. It doesn't need `automodel.cpp` at all, and #791 removes it.

items.title: whisper_npu: WhisperEncoder::add_bias_optimized leaks 1,331,200 B on every encode_audio() call
items.body:
## Summary

Every call to `whisper_npu::encode_audio()` leaks **1,331,200 bytes**. The allocations all come from a single `operator new[]` inside `WhisperEncoder::add_bias_optimized()` that has no matching `delete[]`.

The buffer looks like per-call scratch for the bias broadcast. It survives every teardown path — engine destruction included — because nothing holds a pointer to it after the call returns. At ~1.3 MB per 30 s encode window that is roughly **160 MB per hour of continuous speech**, growing without bound.

**Component:** `whisper_npu` prebuilt engine — affects both `src/lib/hrx/libwhisper_npu.so` and `src/lib/xrt/libwhisper_npu.so` (and the matching `.dll`s).
**Model exercised:** `whisper-v3:turbo` (Whisper-V3-Turbo-NPU2, 32 encoder layers).

## Measurement

heaptrack, comparing a 10-encode run against a 40-encode run of the same audio. Leaked bytes scale linearly and exactly with encode count. Decode steps and `clear_context()` leak nothing, which isolates it to the encode path.

Per encode, 33 allocations:

| count | size each | subtotal |
|------:|----------:|---------:|
| 32 (one per encoder layer) | 40,960 B | 1,310,720 B |
| 1 | 20,480 B | 20,480 B |
| | **total** | **1,331,200 B** |

## Static confirmation from the shipped binaries

This is verifiable from the released artifacts alone — no source needed.

The symbol is local, hence absent from the dynamic table:

```
$ nm -C src/lib/hrx/libwhisper_npu.so | grep add_bias
0000000000028660 t WhisperEncoder::add_bias_optimized(buffer<bfloat16_t>&, buffer<bfloat16_t>&, buffer<bfloat16_t>&) [clone .isra.0]
```

The function spans `0x28660`–`0x289d0`. Every call instruction in that range:

```
$ objdump -d -C --start-address=0x28660 --stop-address=0x289d0 \
      src/lib/hrx/libwhisper_npu.so | grep -oE 'call.*<.*>'
      3  __assert_fail@plt
      1  operator new[](unsigned long)@plt
```

No `operator delete[]`, no `free`, no destructor call. The allocation at `0x286d0` has no release path at all:

```
286c5:  lea    0x0(,%r15,4),%rdi        ; byte count = element_count * 4  (float32 scratch)
286cd:  mov    %r8,%r12
286d0:  call   f040 <operator new[](unsigned long)@plt>
286d5:  mov    %rax,%rdi                ; result used directly, never stored for cleanup
```

Library-wide the imbalance comes down to this one site:

```
$ objdump -d -C src/lib/hrx/libwhisper_npu.so | grep -c 'operator new\[\](unsigned long)@plt'
14
$ objdump -d -C src/lib/hrx/libwhisper_npu.so | grep -c 'operator delete\[\](void\*)@plt'
13
```

14 array allocations against 13 array frees. The one unmatched `new[]` is the one above. The same unmatched allocation is present in the XRT build at `0x57df0`.

The `lea (,%r15,4)` gives a 4-byte element, i.e. a float32 scratch buffer: 40,960 B = 10,240 floats per encoder layer (×32), and 20,480 B = 5,120 floats once per encode.

## Suggested fix

Allocate the scratch once and reuse it. Best as a `WhisperEncoder` member sized at construction — the shapes are fixed per model — which also removes 33 allocator round-trips from the per-encode hot path. Failing that, a `std::vector<float>` / `std::unique_ptr<float[]>` local would at least bound the lifetime to the call.

## Why this needs an engine rebuild

`whisper_npu` ships only as a prebuilt binary (`src/CMakeLists.txt` resolves it out of `${FLM_ENGINE_LIB_DIR}`), and no `WhisperEncoder` source exists in the tree. Unlike `gemma4e_npu`, which has an opt-in source build under `src/detail/` behind `FLM_BUILD_GEMMA4E`, there is no whisper equivalent. The implementation is fully behind the pimpl in `src/include/whisper/whisper_npu.hpp`, so there is no caller-side workaround.

## Possible relation to #585

#585 reports `flm serve --asr 1` with `whisper-v3:turbo` exiting with code -1 after ~2.5–2.8 h, consistently. An unbounded encode-path leak is an obvious suspect, and a single 100 MB audio file is on the order of a hundred encode windows (~138 MB), so the growth can be fast for large inputs.

That said, the evidence does not cleanly line up and I do not want to overclaim: #585 reports uptimes clustering tightly in a 2h28m–2h48m band **regardless of load**, including while idle. A per-encode leak is load-dependent, so heavy-file periods should die noticeably sooner than idle ones. That argues for a time- or handle-based cause as the primary driver, with this leak at most a contributor. Worth checking RSS against uptime on an affected host to separate the two.

---

Found while investigating a separate HRX runtime retention problem (#787).

items.title: hrx: give the runtime a real shutdown path
items.body:
## Problem

Destroying FLM's engines frees FLM's own buffers, but libhrx keeps a 64-entry free-buffer cache plus an internal arena on top, with no call to trim them. A model unload leaves several hundred MiB charged to the process until exit.

`hrx::Runtime` had `ensure()` and no teardown — no destructor, no `shutdown()`.

## Change

`~Runtime()` purges the executable cache, clears the coherence map, releases the stream, and calls `hrx_gpu_shutdown()`. `Runtime::get()` is a function-local static, so this fires automatically during static destruction at process exit, after every engine object is already gone. No caller has to invoke anything.

(An earlier revision instead called a manual `flm_rt_ctl::release_runtime()` from every model-switch site. Per review: a destructor is the right-sized fix, so that's scoped down to just this.)

**Trade-off:** `flm serve` swaps models within one process, and this version only reclaims on process exit — a long-running serve process that switches models repeatedly keeps paying the driver cache cost per switch, as before this PR. A follow-up could call shutdown at switch sites if that matters in practice.

## Reviewer notes

- The cache purge ignores refcounts on purpose — `build_or_get_executable()`'s refcount-free path leaves `refs == 0` entries that a normal sweep would never erase.
- No `hrx_device_release()` call — `hrx_gpu_shutdown()` already owns that reference; releasing it too would be an over-release.
- `hrx::Runtime::get()::r` is `STB_GNU_UNIQUE` in the engine `.so`s, so despite being header-only it's genuinely one instance process-wide.

## Verification

Tested on real amdxdna hardware, against both the pin this PR opened against (v2026.09.15) and the newer pin on `main` (#786, v2026.10.13):

```
after device init             69 MiB   <- libhrx internal arena
after 64 x 8 MiB alloc        581 MiB
after freeing buffers          69 MiB   <- buffer cache (v2026.10.13 improved this)
```

With the destructor firing at exit there's no mid-process state to measure, so the destruction-order precondition was checked directly instead: a test program builds the device + 64 buffers in a scope that ends before `main()` returns, then exits cleanly with `~Runtime()` firing only after `main()` has returned.

**Not covered:** end-to-end model switch (no models on the test machine) and the XRT branch (no XRT headers here, though its body is an empty inline).

items.title: [Issue]: HRX preview (v1.0.8, Linux): flm bench gemma4-it:e2b fails at 32k with 'ert state 8'; XRT completes, serve works
items.body:
## Summary

With the v1.0.8 HRX preview package on Linux, `flm bench gemma4-it:e2b` aborts in its first stage (32k context) on a Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350 (Krackan Point, XDNA2).
Every dispatch fails with `amdxdna dispatch did not complete: ert state 8`, and the run ends with `hrx_buffer_allocate failed`.
The same bench with the standard XRT package completes all 6 stages on the same machine, same container image, same weights.
HRX otherwise works here: `flm validate` passes and `flm serve` with the same model handles a 31,242-token prompt without errors.
So the failure looks specific to the `flm bench` path (or its 32k stage), not to HRX in general.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Laptop | Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6 (21TBCTO1WW), BIOS R33ET31W (1.14) |
| CPU / iGPU | AMD Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350, 8C/16T, Radeon 860M |
| RAM | 30 GiB |
| NPU | `1022:17f0` rev 0x20 (Strix/Krackan/Strix Halo NPU), aie2p, 8 columns |
| NPU firmware | 1.1.2.64 |
| Host OS / kernel | Slackware 15.0 -current, Linux 7.2.10, in-tree `amdxdna` ("amdxdna version: 0.10" in `flm validate`) |
| Module params present | `aie2_max_col`, `force_cmdlist`, `force_iova`, `tdr_timeout_ms` (values not readable as non-root) |
| Container | Docker 29.3.0, `ubuntu:26.04`, `--device /dev/accel/accel0 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ipc host` |
| FLM | v1.0.8; HRX: `HRX_fastflowlm_1.0.8_linux.tar.gz` (bare Ubuntu, no extra packages); XRT: `fastflowlm_1.0.8_ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb` (system `libxrt2`/`libxrt-npu2` from the Ubuntu archive) |
| Model | `gemma4-it:e2b` (Gemma4-E2B-IT-NPU2), pulled with v1.0.8 |

`flm validate` output (HRX package, container): kernel 7.2.10, NPU `/dev/accel/accel0` with 8 columns, FW 1.1.2.64, amdxdna 0.10, memlock infinity, platform aie2p.

## Reproduce

```bash
docker run --rm --device /dev/accel/accel0 --ulimit memlock=-1 --ipc host \
  -v <HRX_tree>:/opt/flm:ro -v <models>:/app/models:ro -v $PWD/out:/out -w /out \
  -e FLM_MODEL_PATH=/app/models -e FLM_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 \
  ubuntu:26.04 /opt/flm/flm bench gemma4-it:e2b --pmode performance --bench-iterations 2
```

## Result on HRX (invalid)

Reproduced twice with identical output. Log, with the repeated line collapsed:

```
[FLM]  Starting benchmark with 6 stages...
[FLM]  Starting benchmark for 32k and iteration 1...
[hrx][ERROR] run::wait hrx_stream_wait: .../amdxdna/native_linux_kmq.cc:1140: INTERNAL; amdxdna dispatch did not complete: ert state 8   (x515)
[FLM]  Creating checkpoint at context length 31017
[FLM]  	TTFT: 11.7753s, Prefill Speed: 2649.89 tokens/s, Decoding Speed: 253.331 tokens/s
[FLM]  Starting benchmark for 16k and iteration 1...
[hrx][ERROR] ... ert state 8
[FLM]  Failed to allocate hrx::ext::bo: hrx::ext::bo: hrx_buffer_allocate failed
Error: Failed to allocate hrx::ext::bo: hrx::ext::bo: hrx_buffer_allocate failed
```

The "TTFT 11.8 s / 2650 tok/s" line should not be trusted: the dispatches had failed, and the model output is `<unusedNN>` tokens.
The process exits after the 16k stage starts, so no result table is produced.

## Valid results on the same machine

### XRT, `flm bench gemma4-it:e2b --pmode performance --bench-iterations 2` (completes)

| Context | TTFT (s) | Prefill (tok/s) | Decode (tok/s) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1k | 1.623 ± 0.008 | 603.57 ± 3.01 | 23.54 ± 0.01 |
| 2k | 2.494 ± 0.009 | 781.56 ± 2.86 | 22.59 ± 0.05 |
| 4k | 4.542 ± 0.051 | 856.43 ± 9.58 | 21.14 ± 0.05 |
| 8k | 9.136 ± 0.116 | 850.32 ± 10.72 | 18.70 ± 0.04 |
| 16k | 20.697 ± 0.237 | 749.98 ± 8.56 | 15.02 ± 0.01 |
| 32k | 41.140 ± 0.027 | 754.40 ± 0.37 | 10.79 ± 0.02 |

### XRT vs HRX through `flm serve gemma4-it:e2b --ctx-len 32768 --pmode performance` (both complete, HRX has no dispatch errors)

One request per length, `max_tokens=16`, `temperature=0`, numbers from the response `usage` block:

| Prompt tokens | XRT TTFT (s) | HRX TTFT (s) | XRT prefill (tok/s) | HRX prefill (tok/s) | XRT decode (tok/s) | HRX decode (tok/s) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3,487 | 3.79 | 3.96 | 920.8 | 880.4 | 21.8 | 22.1 |
| 10,648 | 14.38 | 15.60 | 740.5 | 682.7 | 17.4 | 16.7 |
| 21,736 | 35.13 | 34.61 | 618.7 | 628.0 | 13.1 | 13.1 |
| 31,242 | 63.29 | 58.48 | 493.6 | 534.2 | 10.8 | 10.8 |

`gemma4-it:12b`, `flm serve --ctx-len 8192`, 24-token prompt, 200 generated tokens, 3 runs each: decode XRT 6.12 / 6.04 / 5.87 tok/s, HRX 6.04 / 5.31 / 5.62 tok/s; TTFT XRT 1.69-1.86 s, HRX 1.85-2.18 s.

Single runs, so roughly ±5% noise. HRX is at parity with XRT in serve mode on this machine.

## Questions

1. Is `flm bench` on HRX known to fail at 32k? `ert state 8` looks like a command timeout; could a single large dispatch in the bench path exceed the amdxdna TDR timeout, while `serve` chunks the prefill differently?
2. Is there a recommended `tdr_timeout_ms` (or other amdxdna module parameter) for the HRX path?
3. Is `--prefill-chunk-len` honoured by `flm bench`? I did not try changing it.

Happy to run more tests (other models, `--prefill-chunk-len`, smaller contexts) and attach full logs.

items.title: fix: stop gpt-oss router bias load from reading past the tensor
items.body:
Updates the gpt-oss NPU libraries for both backends with the fix from the internal PR:

- `src/lib/hrx/gpt_oss_npu.dll`
- `src/lib/hrx/libgpt_oss_npu.so`
- `src/lib/xrt/gpt_oss_npu.dll`
- `src/lib/xrt/libgpt_oss_npu.so`

## Fix
`load_weights` copied the 4096-byte device slot out of the 32-bf16 `router.bias` tensor. That read walks off the 64-byte allocation and faults in `memcpy` when the buffer ends on an uncommitted page, which results in an occasional gpt-oss-sg access violation. The load now copies the real tensor and zeroes the rest of the slot.

items.title: fix(server): make model switching in serve leave consistent state
items.body:
## Summary

Long sweeps through many models in one `flm serve` process could fail on later models while each model worked on its own. This fixes the bugs on the model-switch path, focused on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`.

- **Prefill chunk length is set per model.** It was latched from the first model loaded. `gemma4e-flash`, `qwen3vl-flash` and `hy-mt2-flash` use 1024-token chunks and everything else uses 4096, so after any ordinary model the flash models were fed 4096-token chunks. `--prefill-chunk-len` still overrides it.
- **A failed switch no longer leaves a stale tag.** The old engine was released before the new one loaded, but on an incompatible model, a failed download or an exception from `get_auto_model`, `current_model_tag` still named the old model. The next request for it skipped the reload and called into an unloaded or null engine. Nothing is now marked loaded until the new load succeeds, and download failures and incompatibility are reported instead of ignored.
- **Aliases don't reload every request.** The check compared the raw request tag (`Ollama/llama3.2:1b`, `llama3.2`) with the resolved one.
- **`PromptCache::reset()` forces a miss, as its comment says.** Empty checksums matched any conversation, so the next multi-turn request set `restore_allowed` on an engine with no checkpoint. In the llama and gemma4e frontends, `restore()`'s `-1` then went into the unsigned `total_tokens`, and the request failed with "Max length reached". A reload now resets the cache, which replaces the function-static `model_used_for_last_message`. `/v1/completions` also resets it, since it reuses the same engine.
- **`/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` honour `"backend"`,** as `docs/instructions/cli.md` already says they do.
- **`~AutoModel` releases the engine before the xclbin manager.** Default member order freed the hardware contexts first, while the engine's `npu_app`s still held raw pointers into them.

## Testing

- `flm` builds in Release (MSVC, XRT).
- The ordering checks in `test_gemma4_backend.cpp` that read `ensure_model_loaded`'s source still pass when re-run against the edited function.
- **Not yet run on hardware.** Suggested sweep on `/v1/chat/completions`:
  1. Start on `llama3.2:1b`, then switch to `qwen3vl-flash:4b` with a prompt over 1024 tokens. The log should show 1024-token prefill chunks.
  2. Send `Ollama/llama3.2:1b` twice. It should load once.
  3. Request an unavailable `"backend"`, then send a request with no `model`. Expect an error, not a crash.
  4. Send a `/v1/completions` call, then a multi-turn chat. The chat should be a cache miss with a correct answer.

## Not in this PR

- The llama and gemma4e frontends still assign an unguarded `restore()` result to `total_tokens` (qwen3 checks it).
- `flm run`'s `/load` has the same latched chunk-size bug.
- The Ollama endpoints get the shared `ensure_model_loaded` fixes but don't reset the chat cache.

items.title: fix(qwen3.5): capture logprobs on the prefill draw when the think block is prefilled
items.body:
## Motivation

This PR brings #777 (logprobs, which contains #776) together with
#778 and #779.

With the think block prefilled, the token `_shared_insert()` draws is the
answer's first token. #777 arms the capture only in `generate()`, on the old
path, and `_shared_insert()` disarms at its top. So a single-turn model
returned no logprobs at all.

## Technical Details

**New here is one commit,** `fix(qwen3.5): capture logprobs on the prefill
draw when the think block is prefilled`. `_shared_insert()` takes
`capture_logprobs` and arms the sampler right before its own draw, after the
disarming at its top. `Qwen3_5VL::insert()` passes it, together with
`record_sampled_token`, exactly when the block was prefilled. A thrown-away
draw is never captured.

The other commits are #776, #777, #778 and #779 including
its guard, cherry-picked. Once those are merged this reduces to the one commit,
and I'll rebase.

## Test Plan

- The same binary with and without the `single-turn` label, so only the
  prefill path differs. 20 one-token prompts, `temperature: 0`,
  `logprobs: true, top_logprobs: 3`.
- Shape: a multi-token answer, a request without logprobs, `think: true`.
- A real workload: a decision-game client running against this build.

## Test Result

```
                                     without label    with single-turn
median wall                          572 ms           455 ms
completion_tokens (max_tokens=1)     1                1
logprobs entries / chosen = content  1 / yes          1 / yes
20-token answer                      16 entries for 17 tokens (EOS gets none), both
no logprobs / think: true            null / null, both
```

Against `main` (604 ms) that is −149 ms, about 25 %. Answers differ in 1 of 20
prompts, the exact tie from #<prefill PR>. The log-odds between options shift
by 0.25 nats median, 0.5 at most.

**Real workload.** A decision game made 170 decisions against this build, many
of them identical requests in a row. There was no crash, and in-game latency
went from 936 to 774 ms compared with #776 + #777 alone. No accuracy change is
claimed here: answers and latency changed together, and the game is
time-sensitive.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

items.title: perf(qwen3.5): prefill the empty think block for single-turn models
items.body:
## Motivation

Without thinking, the Qwen3.5 chat template ends with an empty think block,
`<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`. `Qwen3_5VL::insert()` cuts those four tokens off
before the prefill, so the checkpoint lands where the next turn of a
conversation diverges. `generate()` then feeds them in with one `forward()`
each. Only after those four decode steps comes the draw for the answer's first
token.

A single-turn model never returns to that checkpoint, so the four decode steps
buy nothing. On Qwen3.5-2B they are ~118 ms of a ~600 ms one-token request.
The decision models from #776 and #777 are single-turn by nature.

## Technical Details

- **The change.** For `single_turn && !enable_think`, `insert()` prefills the
  block together with the prompt. The token `_shared_insert()` draws from the
  prefill logits is the answer's first token, and `generate()` takes
  `last_token` instead of running the forced block. Multi-turn models keep the
  old path, because there the checkpoint pays off. So does `think: true`.
- **Opt-in per catalog entry.** The existing `"single-turn"` label now also
  sets `AutoModel::single_turn` (in `_shared_initialize_model_state()`). Until
  now only the hunyuan, `Qwen3VL_Flash` and gemma4e classes set the flag
  themselves, and their catalog entries already carry the label, so nothing
  changes for them. The flag is only ever switched on, never off. **Models
  without the label run exactly the old path.** The label keeps its existing
  effects: `/v1/chat/completions` rejects requests with assistant messages,
  and a context-length override is ignored.
- **Second commit: prefill again when a request matches the whole history.**
  With the block prefilled, a single-turn request puts exactly its own tokens
  into `token_history`. If the same request comes again and nothing is left to
  prefill, `_chunked_insert()` returns an empty buffer and `Sampler::sample()`
  reads it, which is a segfault at address 0. This PR alone cannot hit it,
  because the decode loop still appends one more token. Together with
  #<max_tokens PR> it can. A complete match is now treated like a divergence.
  Stepping back by one token is not possible, because the linear attention
  layers carry recurrent state.

**Numerics.** The template's four tokens are exactly the ids `generate()` used
to feed: `[248068, 271, 248069, 271]`, checked with the model's tokenizer. They
now go through the prefill kernels instead of four decode steps, so the result
is not bit-identical; see Test Result. Neither path is a reference, since the
prompt itself always runs through the prefill kernels.

With #777, the first answer token is now drawn in `_shared_insert()`, where
#777 does not capture. That is handled in #<combined PR>.

## Test Plan

- **Latency.** Same harness as #<max_tokens PR>: 20 independent one-token
  prompts, `temperature: 0`, three alternating rounds of `main` against this
  branch, with the label set in a copy of the catalog.
- **Answers.** This branch against `main` + #776. `main`'s own answers are
  distorted by the discarded-sample penalty that #776 removes.
- **Tokenization** of the template tail.
- **Crash.** The same request twice, with this branch and the max_tokens fix
  combined, under gdb. Then eight identical requests in a row with the guard.

## Test Result

```
                      main      this PR
median wall           604 ms    486 ms
prefill_duration      430 ms    431 ms
decoding_duration     117 ms     30 ms   (what is left is the max_tokens off-by-one)
```

**Answers.**

- Against `main`, the first letter differs in 16 of 20 prompts. That is the
  penalty #776 removes, not this change.
- Against `main` + #776, 1 of 20 differs. That one was an exact tie: A and C
  were both at logprob −1.939 on the old path.
- One of two 60-token generations diverges after 90 characters.
- With #777 on top, the log-odds between options move by 0.25 nats median, 0.5
  at most.

**Crash.** With this PR and #<max_tokens PR> combined, the second identical
request segfaulted in `Sampler::sample()` called from `_shared_insert()`. Its
log shows no `Prefill chunk` line. With the guard, eight identical requests in
a row pass, answers and confidences are unchanged, and the extra prefill is
not measurable.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

items.title: fix(qwen3.5): stop at max_tokens instead of one token past it
items.body:
## Motivation

`Qwen3_5VL::generate()` draws the first token before its decode loop and
checked `max_tokens` only at the bottom of the loop, after the next draw. Every
request that runs into the limit gets one token more than it asked for and pays
one more `forward()` for it: `max_tokens=1` returns `"A\n"` with
`completion_tokens: 2`.

For a model that answers with a single token, that is the whole request: an
extra decode step, and a trailing token the caller has to strip. The Qwen3.5
fine-tunes from #776 and #777 hit it on every call:

- [seimanu/decider-0.8b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-0.8b-NPU2)
- [seimanu/decider-2b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-2b-NPU2)
- [seimanu/decider-4b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-4b-NPU2)

## Technical Details

The loop is now `while (true)` and checks the limit first, before it draws. It
has the same shape as `_shared_generate()`: the context limit is checked inside
the loop, and reaching `max_tokens` still wins over it. So `finish_reason` is
unchanged even when both limits are hit at once.

Independent of #776 and #777; applies to `main` as is.

**Scope.** Only `Qwen3_5VL::generate()`. Two other places have the same
pattern. They are left for separate changes:

- `Qwen3_6_MOE::generate()` has the same loop, with the limit checked after the
  draw. I found this by reading only; it is not changed here, because I could
  not test that model.
- `_shared_generate()` emits the token drawn in `_shared_insert()` without
  counting it. There `max_tokens=N` returns N+1 tokens while `usage` reports N.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.5-2B (`decider-2b-NPU2`) on a Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350, `platform_profile`
performance. The prompt set is 20 independent one-token decision prompts with
no shared prefixes, `temperature: 0`. Three alternating rounds of `main`
against this branch, one server start per variant and round, wall clock per
request. Plus two 60-token generations, compared character by character.

## Test Result

```
                    main      this PR
median wall         604 ms    574 ms
completion_tokens   2         1
content             "B\n"     "B"
```

Per-round medians: 604 / 605 / 602 ms against 574 / 574 / 575 ms. The first
token of all 20 answers and both 60-token generations are identical to `main`.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

items.title: feat(server): report logprobs when the request asks for them
items.body:
## Motivation

`/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` write a hard-coded
`{"logprobs", nullptr}` into their responses. The sampler already keeps the
top-k of every sampled token -- token id, logit and probability -- but nothing
carries them to the response.

A model that answers with a single token -- a classifier, a router, a decision
model -- is unreadable without that distribution. The caller gets the chosen
option and cannot tell whether the model was certain or guessing. Three
Qwen3.5 fine-tunes converted for the NPU hit exactly this, and each of them
was built and measured against this patch:

- [seimanu/decider-0.8b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-0.8b-NPU2)
- [seimanu/decider-2b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-2b-NPU2)
- [seimanu/decider-4b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-4b-NPU2)

Their model cards carry the flm commit they were tested with and the
configuration that produced the numbers below.

## Technical Details

Builds on #776. Until that one is merged this PR shows both commits; it exists
because without the fix the reported distribution would include the penalty of
a sample the model never used.

```
sampler.hpp/.cpp    capture_if_requested(), log_sum_exp_all() and a table of
                    exp() for every bf16 value; the sampling paths capture
                    once per draw while a request has the sampler armed
automodel.hpp/.cpp  top_logprob_t, logprobs_entry_t,
                    _request_logprobs_capture() and _record_top_logprobs()
modeling_qwen3_5vl  records where a token reaches the caller's text, not where
                    it was drawn
rest_handler.cpp    reads the request, builds both response shapes
```

**One entry per token of `message.content`**, in the same order, so a client
that pairs entries with tokens stays aligned. Recording happens where the token
is written to the response, which is what keeps the two in step: a token the
engine filters out gets no entry, and neither does EOS. A 17-token answer comes
back with 16 entries. An answer that carries a tool call gets `null`, because
`message.content` is empty and there are no tokens to describe.

**`logprob` is a real log-probability** -- logit minus logsumexp over the whole
vocabulary, after the penalties and before the temperature. It is not
renormalised over the entries listed, so those do not sum to 1; the rest of the
vocabulary lies outside the list.

**The logsumexp is exact and cheap.** The logits arrive as bf16 from the
engine, so there are only 65536 possible values, and a table of `exp()` for
each of them (512 KB, fits in L2) replaces a quarter of a million `exp()` calls
with as many reads. Values the penalties moved off the bf16 grid take the exact
call. The result differs from the shifted computation by about one float ulp,
which is rounding, not approximation. For the alternatives, `N <= top_k` needs
no sort at all: `top_k_logits` is already sorted by logit with the same
tie-break, so its beginning is the top-n.

**The two request shapes differ, as they do upstream:** chat takes `logprobs`
as a boolean plus `top_logprobs` (0-20), completions takes `logprobs` as an
integer 0-5 and has no `top_logprobs`. For completions 0 is a valid request: it
asks for the drawn token's own logprob with no alternatives.

**A request that does not ask pays nothing.** The sampler is disarmed at the
start of every request, before anything that can return early; it is armed only
in Qwen3.5-VL's `generate()`, and only when the request asks for logprobs.

Seen while testing this, not touched here: a model that emits half a
multi-byte character crashes the endpoint. `nlohmann::json` throws while
serialising the response text --

```
[json.exception.type_error.316] incomplete UTF-8 string; last byte: 0x98
```

-- and the request fails with a 500. It happens without `logprobs` too, so it
is not from this patch; the guard in `_record_top_logprobs` covers the
logprobs path, and the response text has no equivalent.

Limitations, unchanged by this patch:

- only Qwen3.5-VL reports; every other model still returns `null`
- streaming responses carry no logprobs
- with `think: true` the answer gets `null`: the tokens of the reasoning block
  land in `reasoning_content`, not in `content`
- `think` is a setting on the model, not on the request. One request with
  `think: true` leaves every later one in that mode, and they all come back with
  `logprobs: null` until it is set back. That is existing behaviour, but this
  patch is what makes it visible

## Test Plan

- **Shape and alignment:** a multi-token answer, entry count against token
  count; a tool-call answer; `think: true`
- **Invariant:** `top_k=2`, `temperature=1`, 50 runs -- the drawn token must
  appear in its own entry every time
- **Non-ASCII:** a German prompt producing umlauts, then rebuilding each token
  from its `bytes` and comparing
- **Regression:** the same request with and without `logprobs`, text compared
  character by character; then a run of without -> with -> without, to show the
  sampler is disarmed again
- **Cost:** wall clock, 300 tokens, nothing else running

## Test Result

```
17-token answer          16 entries          (EOS gets none)
tool call                logprobs: null
think: true              logprobs: null
top_k=2, temp 1, 50x     50 of 50 in the list
umlauts                  bytes 0-255, every token rebuilds from its bytes
without logprobs         field is null, text unchanged
without -> with -> without   10.23 / 9.98 / 10.25 s, 300 tokens each
```

The cost is inside the run-to-run spread -- the three runs without logprobs
differ by 0.05 s on their own, and the run with logprobs was faster than the
first. The honest figure is: at most about 1 %, and only for requests that ask.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

items.title: fix: don't count a discarded sample as generated text
items.body:
## Motivation

`Qwen3_5VL::insert()` and `Qwen3_6_MoE::insert()` call `_shared_insert()`, which
prefills and draws one token into `last_token`. Their `generate()` then
force-feeds the think block and samples again -- the drawn token is never used,
and the only reference to it is an assert.

`sample()` records every drawn token in the repetition and frequency windows
first. A token that was thrown away therefore counts as generated text. For a
model that answers without a thinking block the token predicted after
`assistant` IS the answer letter, so it is pushed down by
`count * freq_penalty + pre_penalty` at exactly the position where it is
needed -- 1.0 + 1.5 = 2.5 logits with this model's defaults.

The visible effect is that the model answers against its own preference. On
`Write one sentence about the sea.` it says `A vast, ever-changing blue
expanse...` where it says `The sea is a vast, ever-changing blue mirror...`
once the discarded sample is no longer counted. Both are fine sentences; the
second is the one the model chose.

Three Qwen3.5 fine-tunes converted for the NPU are affected directly: they
answer with a single letter, and that letter is the one being pushed down.

- [seimanu/decider-0.8b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-0.8b-NPU2)
- [seimanu/decider-2b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-2b-NPU2)
- [seimanu/decider-4b-NPU2](https://huggingface.co/seimanu/decider-4b-NPU2)

## Technical Details

`Sampler::sample()` and `sample_greedy()` take a `record_in_history` flag,
defaulting to `true`, so no other model changes behaviour. `sample()` forwards
it to `sample_greedy()` on the `top_k == 1` path, and `_shared_insert()` passes
it through from its caller. `Qwen3_5VL::insert()` and `Qwen3_6_MoE::insert()`
pass `false` for the draw they discard.

Both paths have to honour the flag. With only one of them in place the same
prompt answers differently depending on a sampling knob:

```
top_k=1    B     (greedy path)
top_k=40   A     (sampled path)
```

**Scope, and what it does not claim.** Two models are covered, because they are
the two where the draw is provably discarded: in both, `last_token` appears
only in an assert and is read nowhere. The flag defaults to `true`, so every
other model keeps its behaviour -- which also means a model with the same
pattern would keep the bug. Several of them call `_shared_insert()` more than
once per request (qwen3 four times, gemma4e three, qwen3vl three, qwen3_8mtp
three); whether any of those calls throws its draw away needs checking one by
one, and this PR does not claim to have done it.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.5-2B, two prompts that differ in one clause, `temperature: 0`, the same
build settings before and after, both sampling paths:

- `top_k=40, temperature=0` -- the sampled path
- `top_k=1, temperature=0` -- the greedy path, through `sample_greedy()`

## Test Result

Before, both paths and both prompts answered `B`. After, all four answer `A`:

```
        before   after
Q k=1     B        A
Q k=40    B        A
R k=1     B        A
R k=40    B        A
```

`A` is the argmax of the unpenalised distribution (0.339 against 0.299 for
`B`), so the answer is no longer the penalised one.

For text generation the change is visible but harmless: see the two sentences
in the motivation. Nothing else moves -- `record_in_history` defaults to
`true`, and only the two Qwen3.5-VL paths pass `false`.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.
