items.title: refactor(rai): run Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 as corelib's own models
items.body:
Stacked on #774 — review the 9 commits after `abcfa3b4` (`f4c49ab5..1a754611`). Retarget or rebase once #774 lands.

Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 on the `rai` backend stop driving corelib op by op and run as corelib's own models (`ryzenai_corelib_model_*`), the way Qwen3.6 already did. All four now share one engine and one backend; each model is a ~20-line spec. Phi-4 is unchanged (corelib's `phi4mini` takes ONNX only, and FastFlowLM ships a GGUF).

## What changes

**One engine: `flm::rai::CorelibModel`** (`include/rai/corelib_model.hpp`, `common/rai/corelib_model.cpp`)
- A `causal_lm` over a corelib model, generalized from the Qwen3.6 engine. `ModelSpec` states what differs between models:
  - `Continuation` — where a multi-row pass may start past position 0: anywhere (Qwen3.5/3.6), only at 0 (Qwen3, so a later prompt re-runs the conversation), or at 0 / a 4096-row page boundary (Gemma 4).
  - `Rewind` — `kSeek` for attention-only models (every pass states its position; rewind and restore just move it), `kSnapshot` for Qwen3.6 (`model_state_save/restore`), `kReplay` for Qwen3.5 (reset and replay).
- Token ids and the context limit are checked before corelib is called; a failed forward, restore or reset poisons the engine.
- `clear_context` on a `kSeek` model makes no corelib call: a pass never reads the cache past its position, and `model_reset` cost ~60 ms per request on Qwen3.

**One backend: `flm::rai::Factory(BackendSpec)`** (`include/rai/corelib_model_backend.hpp`)
- Refuses preemption and a context outside the model's rule, reads the package's token ids, and resolves the GGUF before the runtime or weights are touched.
- EOS ids are either given (Qwen3, Qwen3.5) or read from the package: `tokenizer_config.json`'s `eos_token` plus `config.json`'s `eos_token_id` (Qwen3.6, Gemma 4 → {1, 106}); Gemma 4's BOS comes from `bos_token`.

**Removed**
- The per-op engines, GGUF readers, shape plans and host math of Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4; `rai/gguf_file`, `rai/weight_cache`, and the Q8/RMSNorm parts of `rai/host_ops`; 14 corelib entry points nothing calls any more.
- There is no packed-weight cache on this path: corelib packs the weights on every load. Old `<gguf stem>.rai-weights.bin/.json` files can be deleted.

**Tests**
- New `src/test/rai_model/`: 36 engine tests (every `Rewind`/`Continuation` combination, poisoning, capacity) and 14 backend tests against the fake corelib. The Qwen3.6 tests moved here.
- Gemma 4's registry, catalog and server-gate tests moved verbatim to `test_gemma4_registry.cpp`, plus one test of the Gemma 4 spec. The op-level Gemma 4 and Qwen3 suites are gone.

Docs: `src/common/models/README.md` gains §2a ("a model corelib runs whole"); the Qwen page notes the dropped weight cache.

## Results (xcomedusad-44, AIE4; old and new builds run interleaved)

| Model | Load, new vs old | Long-prompt TTFT, new vs old | Decode tok/s, new vs old | Greedy text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| qwen3-rai:0.6b | 3.8–4.5 s vs 2.7–3.1 s | 0.25–0.28 vs 0.26–0.39 s | 69–79 vs 62–81 | identical |
| qwen3.5-rai:9b | 11–27 s vs 56 s | 41.8 vs 49.3 s | 13–20 vs 15.6 | identical |
| qwen3.6-moe-rai:35b-a3b | 87–88 vs 92 s | 14.2 vs 14.75 s | 18–20 vs 19 | one near-tie token in 1 of 2 runs |
| gemma4-it-rai:e2b | 7–15 s vs 3.2–4.9 s | 1.17–1.39 vs 0.75–0.94 s | 30.7 vs 40.4 | one near-tie token (old flips it too) |
| gemma4-it-rai:e4b | 12–17 s vs 3.5–5.6 s | 1.95–2.41 vs 1.20–1.24 s | 18.8 vs 26.6 | identical |
| phi4-mini-it-rai:4b (unchanged) | ~same | 0.61–0.63 vs 0.605 s | 35–39 vs 37 | same as old |

- Gemma 4 E2B at 16k: passkey recalled; a short prompt after the full paged cache matches a fresh run.
- Switching e2b → qwen3 → qwen3.5 → e4b → phi4 → e2b in one `flm serve` process: every answer matches a fresh run, no errors.
- Fake-corelib suites: rai_model 2/2, phi4_rai 8/8, gemma4_rai 3/3 (real-package tokenizer test skipped).

**Known regression: Gemma 4 is slower on corelib 0.26's built-in model.** Prefill takes ~1.5× (E2B) / 1.6–2× (E4B), decode is 24–29% slower, and loads are slower. The cause is in corelib, not here: the host per-layer-embedding projection in `Gemma4::BuildPle` (FP32 weights, scalar, single-threaded on decode) and serial weight packing with no pre-packed input. A corelib fix is being prepared; FastFlowLM picks it up with a version bump. Qwen3 loads ~1 s slower without the packed-weight cache.

## Not covered
- Built and tested on Windows only; the Linux build of `flm_rai` was not compiled for this change.

---
**Diff:** 69 files; product code +801 / −8,423, tests +1,487 / −12,763.

items.title: feat(core): move to ryzenai-corelib 0.33.1, run every corelib model behind one engine, prefer AMD Q4 GGUFs, rename rai to core
items.body:
Follow-up to #748. Moves the corelib backend from ryzenai-corelib 0.11 to 0.33.1, adds Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-4B, runs Gemma 4 at 16k and Qwen3.5 at 32k, has every corelib model (Phi-4, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Gemma 4) run as corelib's own model behind one shared engine, makes `flm pull` prefer AMD's Q4 GGUFs with a public Q8_0 fallback, and renames the backend from `rai` to `core`.

> **Breaking rename (commit 6).** The `rai` backend added in #748 becomes `core`, and the `aie_next` platform becomes `dev04`: tags move from `*-rai:*` to `*-core:*` (e.g. `phi4-mini-it-rai:4b` → `phi4-mini-it-core:4b`), `FLM_ENABLE_RAI` → `FLM_ENABLE_CORE`, the `*-rai` presets → `*-core`, `FLM_RAI_*` → `FLM_CORE_*`, `home_install.sh --rai` → `--core`, and `--backend rai` → `--backend core`. No old name is kept as an alias. `ryzenai-corelib` and `RYZENAI_CORELIB_*` name the external library and stay.

Commits:
1. **corelib 0.26, Qwen3.6, Gemma 4 at 16k** on the existing per-op engines.
2. **One engine for corelib's models.** Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 stop driving corelib op by op and run as `ryzenai_corelib_model_*`, like Qwen3.6.
3. **corelib 0.28.** Qwen3.5's KV cache is paged up to 32768, and a later turn's prefill chunks start on 4096-row page boundaries.
4. **corelib 0.29.2.** No ABI change; corelib speeds up Gemma 4's per-layer-embedding projection and runs Qwen3.6's in-page prefill chunks on the NPU.
5. **corelib 0.29.4.** No ABI change; corelib refuses a Qwen3.6 capacity past 131072, the most it has verified on the NPU, so Qwen3.6's limit drops from 262144 to 131072.
6. **Rename `rai` → `core` and `aie_next` → `dev04`**, as above. Directories and files carrying either name move with them; no behaviour change.
7. **corelib 0.29.7.** No ABI change. `src/test/phi4_core`'s version-pin probe can fail again (it used to pass by failing on a missing include path).
8. **`flm pull` prefers AMD Q4 GGUFs** for the core models and falls back to the public Q8_0 source. Adds `qwen3.5-core:4b`.
9. **Phi-4 on corelib's `phi4mini` model**, Q8_0 or Q4_G128; the last per-op engine is removed. Also fixes the token history keeping an EOS the engine never ran.
10. **corelib 0.33.1.** `model_forward`, `forward_options` and `create_stream` change shape.

## Models

Every tag below runs as a corelib model through the shared engine.

| Tag | GGUF (preferred → fallback) | Context | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.6-moe-core:35b-a3b` | unsloth Q8_0 | default 4096, up to 131072 | **New.** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, text only |
| `gemma4-it-core:e2b` `gemma4-it-core:e4b` | AMD Q4_G32 → unsloth Q8_0 | default and max 16384 | Was 4096; E4B is offered again |
| `qwen3-core:0.6b` | unsloth Q8_0 | 4096 | Moved off the per-op engine |
| `qwen3-core:1.7b` `4b` `8b` | AMD Q4_G128 → unsloth Q8_0 | 4096 | Moved off the per-op engine |
| `qwen3.5-core:9b` | AMD Q4_G128 → unsloth Q8_0 | default 4096, up to 32768 | Moved off the per-op engine; was capped at 4096 |
| `qwen3.5-core:4b` | AMD Q4_G128 → unsloth Q8_0 | default 4096, up to 32768 | **New.** A bare `qwen3.5-core` now resolves to `4b` |
| `phi4-mini-it-core:4b` | AMD Q4_G128 → unsloth Q8_0 | 4096 | Moved off the per-op engine; reads Q8_0 or Q4_G128 |

## What changes

**corelib 0.33.1 (version pinned exactly)**
- 0.26: `create_tensor_window` takes `strides`, `linear_attention_bf16` takes `rows`, and models are built with `model_weights_create_path` + `model_create(name, weights, options)`.
- 0.30: `create_stream` takes a priority list of PDIs per phase. `OpenModelStream`, which nothing calls any more, passes its two PDIs as one-element lists.
- 0.31 / 0.33: `model_forward` takes images, options, `out_token` and the logits as arguments, and `forward_options` gains a leading `size` that corelib refuses when short. `CorelibModel` sets `size` and passes its logits buffer only when it wants logits.
- 0.28, 0.29.x and the rest of 0.30–0.33 add nothing FastFlowLM has to meet. 0.31–0.33 add Qwen3.6 image input, which FastFlowLM does not pass.
- `docs/core-setup-linux.md`: `RYZENAI_CORELIB_FALLBACK_PROFILE` is now `RYZENAI_CORELIB_REPORT_FALLBACKS`, and `RYZENAI_CORELIB_TRACE_XRT` is now `RYZENAI_CORELIB_TRACE=xrt`.

**Packaging**
- corelib installs `ryzenai_corelib` plus one `ryzenai_corelib_model_<name>` library per model and loads them only from its own directory. A Windows core build copies them beside `flm.exe`; `home_install.sh` copies them beside corelib on Linux.
- `RYZENAI_CORELIB_DD_ROOT` / `RYZENAI_CORELIB_KERNELS_ROOT` are no longer needed, and the installer stops staging DynamicDispatch.

**One engine: `flm::core::CorelibModel`** (`include/core/corelib_model.hpp`, `common/core/corelib_model.cpp`)
- A `causal_lm` over a corelib model. Each model is a short `ModelSpec` naming what differs:
  - `Continuation`: where a multi-row pass may start past position 0 — anywhere (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6), only at 0 (Qwen3 and Phi-4, so a later prompt re-runs the conversation), or at 0 / a 4096-row page boundary (Gemma 4).
  - `Rewind`: `kSeek` for attention-only models (every pass states its position; rewind just moves it), `kSnapshot` for Qwen3.6 (`model_state_save/restore`, reused only if its history is a prefix of the current one), `kReplay` for Qwen3.5 (reset and replay).
- Token ids and the context limit are checked before corelib is called. A failed forward, restore or reset poisons the engine.
- Logits are fetched only for the row that gets sampled.

**One backend: `flm::core::Factory(BackendSpec)`** (`include/core/corelib_model_backend.hpp`)
- Refuses preemption and a context outside the model's rule, reads the package's BOS/EOS ids (`tokenizer_config.json` + `config.json`, e.g. Gemma 4 → {1, 106}; Phi-4 adds `<|end|>`, which the package does not name), and resolves the GGUF the catalog points at before the runtime or weights are touched. Image requests on core return HTTP 400.

**Preferred AMD sources in `flm pull`** (`model_list.hpp`, `pull/`)
- A catalog entry may carry `preferred_source`, a JSON merge patch over the entry that sets its own `url`, `files`, `size`, quantization level and `model_info_key`. Each AMD source is pinned to a commit, and its GGUF to a sha256 in `model_info.json` (keyed `<tag>@amd`); the tokenizer and config files keep their existing pinned sources.
- `flm pull` sends a HEAD request for the preferred GGUF and uses it on 2xx/3xx; otherwise it prints `Falling back to: <url>` and pulls the entry's own source. Files already on disk are kept without probing.
- Outside a pull, an entry resolves to its preferred source exactly when every file only that source has is on disk, so `run`, `serve`, `list` and `check` follow whatever was pulled.
- The AMD repos currently need a Hugging Face token (`HF_TOKEN`, `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN`, `HF_TOKEN_PATH`, `HF_HOME/token` or `~/.cache/huggingface/token`). It is sent only for a `"use_hf_token": true` source, only to `https://huggingface.co/`, with TLS verification on; public sources never get it. Without access, a pull falls back to the public Q8_0.

**Page-aligned prefill chunks** (`AutoModel::_chunked_insert`, `model_backend.hpp`)
- New `ModelBackend::aligns_prefill_chunks()`, default `false`, so FastFlowLM's own engines are unaffected. The corelib-model backend returns `true`: a later turn's prompt is chunked on multiples of 4096 counted from position 0 instead of from the turn's start, so every chunk after the first starts on a page boundary and corelib runs it as whole pages on the NPU. Prompts carrying a multimodal payload keep the old chunking.

**EOS in the token history** (`AutoModel::_shared_generate`)
- An EOS the engine never ran (sampled straight from the prefill, or ending a decode on a backend that declines the post-EOS forward, which every core backend does) is no longer appended to the token history. Before, the next turn's prefix match treated it as already held, so the engine never saw the end-of-turn token between the reply and the next user message. It is now prefilled with the next turn. A frontend test covers both cases on core and the unchanged behaviour on FastFlowLM's own engines.

**Removed**
- Every per-op engine (Phi-4, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Gemma 4) with its GGUF reader, shape plan, host math and packed-weight cache; `rai/gguf_file`, `rai/weight_cache`, `core/kernel_grid.hpp`, `core/weight_source.hpp`, the Q8/RMSNorm parts of the host ops, and the corelib entry points nothing calls.
- No core model has a packed-weight cache any more: corelib packs weights on every load. Old `*.rai-weights.bin/.json` and `phi4-*-weights.*` files can be deleted.

**Shared**
- `Sampler::sampler_topk_apply` selects top-k with a k-entry heap in one pass instead of `partial_sort`ing a vocab-sized array each token. Same ranking and lowest-id tie rule; checked against the old code on 63 inputs (vocab 1..248320, k = 1/2/20/40, heavy ties).

Docs: `src/common/models/README.md` gains a section on models corelib runs whole; `docs/core-setup-linux.md` and the model pages cover the version, the AMD and public sources, and the dropped weight cache.

## Results

All on a `dev04` NPU, Windows.

**Unit tests** (fake corelib, 0.33.1 headers): `core_model`, `phi4_core`, `gemma4_core` and `model_backend` pass; `test_model_downloader` includes offline `file://` tests for the preferred-source logic. `test_real_corelib` against the 0.33.1 library loads it, matches the version and resolves every entry point. `flm.exe` builds with `FLM_ENABLE_CORE=ON` against 0.33.1.

**Shared engine vs the per-op engines** (measured at commit 4, corelib 0.29.2) — "before" is the first commit's build on corelib 0.26: the per-op engines for Phi-4, Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4, and Qwen3.6 on corelib's model API. Both builds run interleaved, Gemma 4 twice each, with the NPU checked idle before and after every run. Long-prompt TTFT is the median of three ~1.1k-token prompts; decode is the median over three short prompts, 64 greedy tokens each.

| Model | Load, this PR vs before | Long-prompt TTFT, this PR vs before | Decode tok/s, this PR vs before | Greedy text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gemma4-it-core:e2b` | 8.1–11.4 s vs 3.3–4.2 s | 0.64–0.68 vs 0.80–0.82 s | 34.2–36.2 vs 37.1–38.0 | 1 of 3 prompts differs (known near-tie token) |
| `gemma4-it-core:e4b` | 11.2–16.4 s vs 3.4–3.6 s | 1.02–1.06 vs 1.33–1.35 s | 23.5–23.9 vs 23.6–24.2 | identical |
| `qwen3.6-moe-core:35b-a3b` | 83.2 vs 84.4 s | 1.45 vs 14.18 s | 19.1 vs 20.4 | identical |
| `qwen3.5-core:9b` | 22.5 vs 25.1 s | 42.7 vs 49.3 s | 19.0 vs 19.3 | identical |
| `qwen3-core:0.6b` | 3.2 vs 1.8 s | 0.24 vs 0.25 s | 116.4 vs 121.8 | identical |

Loads are slower because corelib packs the weights on every load and this path has no packed-weight cache.

**Phi-4 on corelib's `phi4mini` vs its per-op engine** (commit 9, corelib 0.29.7):

| Run | Load | ~1.1k-token TTFT | Decode tok/s | Passkey at ~3k tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| per-op, Q8_0, cache cold / warm | 61.7 s / 2.0 s | 0.61 s | 40.8 / 44.4 | correct |
| `phi4mini`, Q8_0 | 6.4–7.6 s | 0.59–0.60 s | 39.0–42.6 | correct |
| `phi4mini`, AMD Q4_G128 | 2.0–2.6 s | 0.60–0.61 s | 39.8–42.6 | correct |

Q8_0 gives the same greedy text on both engines. A second turn, which the per-op engine refused (`Phi-4 prefill must start at logical position zero`), now works, and a two-turn passkey is recalled on Q8_0 and Q4_G128.

**corelib 0.33.1 vs 0.29.7**, and **0.29.7 vs 0.29.4** (each pair run interleaved): greedy text and TTFTs match on every model, Phi-4 on both its Q8_0 and Q4_G128 files. Decode and load differences followed run order rather than the build: rerun with the order swapped, the two builds match.

**Two-turn continuation** at `--ctx-len 16384`: turn 1 is ~6.8k tokens carrying a passkey; turn 2 resends it with the reply and adds ~6.9k tokens, chunked on page boundaries (1395 / 4096 / 1414).

| Model | Turn 1 TTFT | Turn 2 TTFT | Passkey |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.6-moe-core:35b-a3b` | 6.4 s | 7.5 s (14.3 s on corelib 0.28) | correct |
| `gemma4-it-core:e2b` | 6.7 s | 17.5 s | correct |

The same chunks and TTFTs within 0.1 s on 0.29.7 and 0.33.1.

**Qwen3.6 at `--ctx-len 131072`** (corelib 0.29.4, 0.29.7 and 0.33.1): turn 1 is 49,917 tokens with a passkey, turn 2 ends at 75,442 tokens; every build recalls the passkey with the same seven turn-2 chunks, turn-2 TTFT 60–65 s.

Measured on the second commit (corelib 0.26):
- Switching e2b → qwen3 → qwen3.5 → e4b → phi4 → e2b in one `flm serve` process: every answer matches a fresh run, no errors.
- Gemma 4 E2B at 16k: passkey recalled; a short prompt after a full paged cache matches a fresh run.

**Long-context passkey recall** (passkey at 45% depth, measured on the first commit):

| Tag | Context | Prompt tokens | Prefill | Decode tok/s | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gemma4-it-core:e2b` | 16384 | 11,329 | 13.5 s (838 tok/s) | 28.9 | correct |
| `gemma4-it-core:e4b` | 16384 | 11,329 | 13.4 s | — | correct |
| `qwen3.6-moe-core:35b-a3b` | 32768 | 23,714 | 932 s (25 tok/s) | 19.7 | correct |

**Gemma 4 on corelib's built-in model.** On corelib 0.26 it was slower than the per-op engine (prefill ~1.5–2×, decode 24–29% slower), because of corelib's host per-layer-embedding projection. corelib 0.29 fixes that projection: prefill is now faster than the per-op engine, and decode is equal on E4B and ~5–8% lower on E2B. Loads stay slower, as above.

## Not done yet

- [ ] Rebuild and rerun the unit tests on top of current `main` (merge was clean; the merged tree has not been built)
- [ ] Linux build of `flm_core` and the `home_install.sh --core` smoke test

items.title: ci: attach the HRX portable packages to releases as a preview
items.body:
## Summary

The HRX portable builds are produced on every CI run but have never been attached to a release. This PR publishes them as a **preview**, next to the default assets:

| Platform | Release asset |
|---|---|
| Linux | `HRX_fastflowlm_<version>_linux.tar.gz` |
| Windows | `HRX_fastflowlm_<version>_windows_amd64.zip` |

The packages use the same layout as the default portable packages, so they install the same way.

## Changes

- **`debian-portable.yml` / `windows-build.yml`:** add a `release-hrx` job on each platform. Each job runs only on tags and needs only its HRX build. It is a separate job, not an extra `needs:` entry on the existing `release` job, so if the preview HRX build fails, the release just goes out without the HRX asset and the default assets are not held back.
- **`debian-portable.yml`, bug fix:** the Linux `release` job downloaded *every* artifact in the run and uploaded `portable/**/*.gz`. The models-from-source build added in #763 runs in that same job, so the next tag would have attached `models-from-source_fastflowlm_<version>_linux.tar.gz` to the release. The HRX tarball would also have been attached whenever its job happened to finish first. The job now downloads the `portable` artifact by name and uploads only `fastflowlm_*_linux.tar.gz`.
- **`model-sweep.yml`:** in release mode (`workflow_dispatch`), the sweep now checks for the `HRX_*` assets and sweeps them when they are present. Before, it always skipped HRX in release mode. In run mode, the HRX sweeps work as before.

## Test plan

- [x] All three workflows parse as YAML.
- [ ] Push a tag to a fork (or a throwaway tag) and confirm the release gets exactly: the default Linux tarball, the Windows zip and MSI, the `.deb`s, and the two `HRX_*` assets. The `models-from-source_*` tarball must not be attached.
- [ ] Dispatch **Model Sweep** against that release and confirm `sweep-linux-hrx` and `sweep-windows-hrx` run.

Rebuilds the generic decoding `layer.xclbin` for 15 models using the **Peano** build (llvm-aie clang/LLD 22.0.0) instead of the **Chess** build.

No functional change — kernel behavior is identical, only the compiler toolchain used to produce the binaries differs.

Follows up #736, which converted a disjoint set of models.

Combined artifacts drop from **6141858 → 3616410 bytes (41% smaller)**, via a correspondingly smaller `aie_partition` section in each file.

| DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B-NPU2 | 421740 | 255724 |

| Llama-3.2-1B-NPU2 | 394203 | 230315 |
| Llama-3.2-3B-NPU2 | 407211 | 240540 |
| Nanbeige4.1-3B-NPU2 | 408732 | 227979 |

| Qwen3-1.7B-NPU2 | 408380 | 237803 |
| Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-NPU2 | 416620 | 250619 |
| Qwen3-4B-NPU2 | 416620 | 250619 |

| Qwen3-8B-NPU2 | 421740 | 255724 |

Qwen3.8-MTP fails above 16K context with MAX_L_LIMIT / attn_layout error

OS: CachyOS Linux
NPU: NPU2

Port: 13305

Problem

The new qwen3.8-mtp:27b model appears to be limited to a maximum context length of 16K on my system.

With no --ctx-len specified, the model starts successfully, but the resulting context is too small for my use case (Hermes sends a prompt/tool context larger than the available context and receives HTTP 400: Max length reached!).

Setting --ctx-len above 16K causes the model to fail during initialization.

For example, with:

--ctx-len 32768

FastFlowLM fails with:

[ERROR] Failed to load model: attn_layout: max_len 32896 puts the deepest pass's replay at 2056 chunks, past the 1024 its 10-bit BD dimension can walk. max_len is at most 16384 (MAX_L_LIMIT).

attn_layout: max_len 131200 ... max_len is at most 16384 (MAX_L_LIMIT)
Important comparison

The same hardware and FastFlowLM installation can run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with:

--ctx-len 131072

without this error.

Therefore this does not appear to be a general 16K context limitation of the Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350 NPU or FastFlowLM on this hardware.

It appears specific to the attention/kernel/layout implementation being used by the new Qwen3.8-MTP model.

Reproduction

Startup command:

flm serve qwen3.8-mtp:27b \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \

If so, is there a different attention implementation/configuration that should be used for long-context Qwen3.8-MTP?

Additional information

This is particularly relevant for tool-calling/agent workloads because the 16K limit is easily exceeded by a large tool schema/system prompt.

The issue does not occur with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on the same machine using a 131072 context, so I believe the issue is specific to the new Qwen3.8-MTP backend rather than the underlying NPU hardware.

items.title: flm serve: a client that resets before accept stops the server accepting connections (HttpSession ctor throws ENOTCONN)
items.body:
### What happens

If a client connects and then resets the connection (RST) before `flm serve`'s accept handler runs, the server stops accepting new connections until it is restarted. The listening socket stays open, so new clients complete the TCP handshake into the backlog and then hang.

### Cause

`WebServer::do_accept` counts the connection, builds the session, and only then re-arms itself ([`server.cpp:568-590`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L568-L590)):

```cpp
active_connections_.fetch_add(1);
auto session = std::make_shared<HttpSession>(std::move(socket), *this);
session->start(cors);
...
if (running) {
    do_accept();
}
```

The `HttpSession` constructor calls the throwing overloads `socket_.set_option(...)` and `socket_.remote_endpoint()` ([`server.cpp:175-186`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L175-L186)). On Linux, `accept()` still returns a socket that was reset while it sat in the accept queue, but `getpeername()` on it fails with `ENOTCONN`, so `remote_endpoint()` throws. That exception:

1. escapes the accept completion handler before `do_accept()` re-arms, so no further connection is ever accepted;
2. escapes after the `fetch_add`, so the connection slot is never released (see also #680);
3. escapes `ioc.run()`, ending that I/O thread. The per-thread catch logs `Error in WebServer I/O thread: ...` ([`server.cpp:507`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L507)).

The window is between the connection landing in the accept queue and the handler reaching the constructor. It widens whenever I/O threads are busy, for example during NPU work.

### Repro

The socket behaviour, on Linux 7.2:

```python
import socket, struct, time
srv = socket.socket(); srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)); srv.listen(8)
c = socket.create_connection(srv.getsockname())
c.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0)); c.close()
time.sleep(0.2)
a, _ = srv.accept()   # succeeds
a.getpeername()       # OSError: [Errno 107] Transport endpoint is not connected
```

A deterministic way to hit it in `flm serve`, with no timing luck needed:

1. Start `flm serve llama3.2:1b` and wait for `GET /api/version` to answer.
2. `kill -STOP <flm pid>`. The kernel still completes handshakes into the backlog.
3. Connect to the port, set `SO_LINGER {1, 0}`, and close. This queues a reset connection.
4. `kill -CONT <flm pid>`.
5. `GET /api/version` now hangs, and the log shows `Error in WebServer I/O thread: remote_endpoint: Transport endpoint is not connected`.

The socket behaviour above was verified on our Strix Halo host. We are measuring the full `flm serve` sequence now, together with a fix; the code path was read on `main` at 39ff855.

### Suggested fix

- In the constructor, use the `error_code` overloads of `set_option` and `remote_endpoint`, and log "Remote endpoint unavailable" on error, as `close_connection` and `read_request` already do. The session then ends through the normal read-error path.
- In `do_accept`, also wrap session creation and `start()` in a `try`/`catch` that gives the slot back and falls through to the re-arm. Then no future throw during session setup can stop the accept loop.

We'll link our patch here once it is tested.

items.title: flm serve error responses: sent with HTTP 200, include raw exception text, and GET /api/ps is undefined behaviour with no model loaded
items.body:
Three smaller problems in how `flm serve` reports errors. They are grouped here because they share a code path and a fix. Each item says whether it was measured or read from source.

### 1. Error bodies are sent with HTTP 200

`send_response` maps `error.code` to a status only when it equals 400 ([`server.cpp:733-744`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L733-L744)). Everything else is sent as 200:

- the three OpenAI-shaped bodies with `"code": 500` ([`rest_handler.cpp:1326-1331`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1326-L1331), [`:1389-1394`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1389-L1394), [`:1524-1529`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1524-L1529))
- every bare-string `{"error": "..."}`. There are about 30 of these, including `"Failed to load X model!"` (`:659`, `:772`, `:1124`, `:1424`), `"Max length reached"`, and every handler `catch`. For a bare string, `response_data["error"].contains("code")` is simply false.

For example, with no embedding model loaded, `POST /v1/embeddings {"model":"embed-gemma:300m","input":"x"}` answers 200 with a `null` body ([`:921-924`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L921-L924)).

Measured: `POST /v1/embeddings {"input":"probe"}` answers HTTP 200 with `{"error":"[json.exception.type_error.302] type must be string, but is invalid"}`. OpenAI SDKs, and proxies such as lemonade, treat a 200 as success, so the error reaches the user as a malformed success.

### 2. Raw `e.what()` is copied into the response body

Almost every handler `catch` returns `{"error": e.what()}`, and `process_task` returns `"Handler exception: " + e.what()` ([`server.cpp:787`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L787)). There are about 25 sites in `rest_handler.cpp`, for example [`:636`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L636), [`:750`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L750), [`:869`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L869) and [`:1328`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1328). For nlohmann errors this is library-internal text, and a parse error quotes the request's own bytes. That quoting is also what turns an invalid UTF-8 body into a second throw (see #756).

Measured bodies:

```
POST /api/chat {"model":"llama3.2:1b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"options":"x"}
{"error":"[json.exception.type_error.306] cannot use value() with string"}

POST /v1/chat/completions {"model":"llama3.2:1b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":"yes"}
{"error":{"message":"[json.exception.type_error.302] type must be boolean, but is string","type":"server_error","code":500}}
```

Given item 1, stock v1.0.6 sends both with HTTP 200.

### 3. `GET /api/ps` with no chat model loaded is undefined behaviour

`flm serve` started without a tag sets `current_model_tag` to the `model-faker` sentinel ([`main.cpp:545-547`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/src/main.cpp#L545-L547), [`rest_handler.cpp:369`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L369)). So does a failed load ([`:411`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L411)), and the tag stays there until the first load finishes. `handle_ps` passes the sentinel to `get_model_info` ([`:1017`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1017)). That reaches `rectify_model_tag`, which indexes the const `config["models"]["model-faker"]` ([`model_list.hpp:128`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/include/model_list.hpp#L128)): `operator[]` on a const json with a missing key.

Measured on halo: the response is `{"error":"[json.exception.invalid_iterator.207] cannot use key() for non-object iterators"}`. Expected: `{"models": []}`.

### Fixes we are carrying

- Status mapping: numeric `error.code` in the 400-599 range becomes the status, a `server_error` type maps to 500, and every other error shape defaults to 400. See https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/server-error-handling.patch. OpenFlowLM-Next has a fuller `openai_compat::status_for()` (Vegard Berget), which maps OpenAI error types and treats a bare string as 500.
- Exception text: one `exception_error(where, e, request_fault)` helper logs `e.what()` server-side and returns a fixed `invalid_request_error` or `server_error` body. See https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/no-exception-text.patch.
- `/api/ps`: list the chat model only when an engine is loaded and the tag is a supported one. See https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/ps-loaded-models.patch.

One thing to watch when classifying 4xx against 5xx: non-streaming `/api/chat` wraps `generate_with_prompt()`, which does both prefill and decode, in one `catch` ([`rest_handler.cpp:834-840`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L834-L840)). One status can't cover both a chat-template rejection (a client error) and a decode fault (a server error). We tell them apart by whether `meta_info.prompt_tokens` has been set (https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/chat-decode-fault.patch).

The patches are layered on top of each other, so the context lines won't match upstream exactly.

### Environment

FLM v1.0.6 built from the tag, with downstream patches. The bodies quoted above come from upstream code. The HTTP status of each measured response depends on which patches were applied at the time, so statuses are given here from `server.cpp:733-744`, not from the measurements.
Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo), XDNA2 NPU, 8 columns. NixOS, Linux 7.2.8, amdxdna 0.10, NPU FW 1.1.2.65.

items.title: flm serve: /v1/completions, /api/generate and /api/chat keep decoding after the client disconnects
items.body:
Everything below comes from reading the source on `main` at 39ff855. None of it has been measured.

### What looks wrong

The server creates a `CancellationToken` for every request. The token is cancelled when the client socket closes ([`server.cpp:357-388`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L357-L388)) or when `/api/cancel` is called. `/v1/chat/completions` uses it: it calls `cancellation_token->reset()` and passes `[&] { return cancellation_token->cancelled(); }` to both `insert()` and `generate()` ([`rest_handler.cpp:1194-1236`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1194-L1236), [`:1257-1288`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1257-L1288)).

The other generation routes accept the token and never read it:

- `/v1/completions`: `insert()` and `generate()` at [`:1445`, `:1459`, `:1476`, `:1490`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1445-L1490)
- `/api/generate`: [`:677`, `:691`, `:710`, `:724`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L677-L724)
- `/api/chat`: streaming at [`:793`/`:807`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L793-L807). Non-streaming uses `generate_with_prompt()` ([`:835`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L835)), which has no cancellation parameter at all ([`automodel.hpp:434`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/include/AutoModel/automodel.hpp#L434)).

So if a client drops mid-request on one of these routes, the server should keep decoding to `max_tokens` / `num_predict` (default 4096). For `/api/generate` and `/api/chat`, that also holds the NPU lock and blocks the queue behind it. `/v1/completions` isn't queued at all (see #759). `/api/cancel` has no effect on these routes for the same reason.

### Expected

Cancelling on disconnect behaves the same on every generation route as it does on `/v1/chat/completions`.

### Suggested fix

In each of these handlers, call `cancellation_token->reset()` and pass the same `[&] { return cancellation_token->cancelled(); }` predicate to `insert()` and `generate()`, as `handle_openai_chat_completion` does. Non-streaming `/api/chat` would need either a predicate on `generate_with_prompt()` or a switch to `insert()` + `generate()`. The second option changes output for Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6-MoE and GPT-OSS, whose `generate_with_prompt()` differs from that pair.

A probe that closes the connection mid-stream should confirm it: `eval_count` in the log stops short, and `NPU Lock Released!` follows promptly. We haven't run it yet.

### Environment

Found by reading the source; checked against `main` at 39ff855 and v1.0.6.

Related, but a different resource: #680, where client aborts leak connection slots.

items.title: flm serve: /v1/completions and other routes run outside the NPU queue and race with model swaps
items.body:
Everything below comes from reading the source on `main` at 39ff855. None of it has been measured.

### What looks wrong

`requires_npu_access()` decides which requests go through the single NPU queue ([`server.cpp:160-170`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L160-L170)). It lists `/api/generate`, `/api/chat`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/embeddings`. Every other route runs directly on whichever of the 10 I/O threads accepted it ([`main.cpp:624`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/src/main.cpp#L624)), concurrently with whatever holds the NPU. Three of those routes touch state that the queued routes change:

1. **`POST /v1/completions`** is missing from the list, but it does inference. `handle_openai_completion` calls `ensure_model_loaded()`, `insert()` and `generate()` on the shared `auto_chat_engine` ([`rest_handler.cpp:1423-1490`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1423-L1490)). A `/v1/completions` request that arrives while a `/v1/chat/completions` request is decoding would therefore run on the same engine and the same NPU at the same time. If it names a different model, it would reset the engine that the other request is using ([`:385-388`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L385-L388)).
2. **`POST /api/embeddings`** is also missing, while its twin `/v1/embeddings` is listed. Both call the same `handle_embeddings`, which runs the embedding model on the NPU.
3. **`GET /api/ps`** reads `current_model_tag` ([`:1017-1022`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1017-L1022)). Meanwhile, `ensure_model_loaded` assigns that `std::string` on a queued request's thread ([`:411`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L411), [`:418`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L418)). A concurrent read of a `std::string` during assignment is a data race, and undefined behaviour in C++.

   We have measured one consequence on our patched build. The tag stays at the `model-faker` sentinel until a first load finishes. Polling `/api/ps` while that load ran hit the sentinel lookup (a separate bug: undefined behaviour in `rectify_model_tag`) on 19 of 23 polls.

### Expected

Anything that uses or swaps `auto_chat_engine` or the embedding engine goes through the NPU queue. For a read-only route like `/api/ps`, a snapshot of (engine loaded, tag) published under a mutex, or atomically, would be enough.

### Suggested fix

- Add `/v1/completions` and `/api/embeddings` to `requires_npu_access()`.
- Give `/api/ps` a synchronised view of the loaded tag.

We have not written a patch for this yet. We found it while fixing `/api/ps` downstream. That fix (https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/ps-loaded-models.patch) avoids the sentinel lookup, but it does not add synchronisation.

The heap-corruption reports in #608 involve concurrent requests. We haven't connected them to this, so this is only a pointer.

### Environment

Found by reading the source; checked against `main` at 39ff855 and v1.0.6.

items.title: /v1/embeddings ignores prompt_name / task_type, so every input is embedded as a query
items.body:
### What happens

`/v1/embeddings` and `/api/embeddings` always embed with `task_query`, whatever the request asks for. For embed-gemma this silently selects the wrong prefix. A retrieval index built through the server stores every document with the query prefix (`task: search result | query: `) instead of `title: none | text: `.

```bash
flm serve llama3.2:1b --embed 1
for t in query document; do
  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1/embeddings -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"embed-gemma:300m\",\"input\":\"The capital of France is Paris.\",\"prompt_name\":\"$t\"}" \
    | jq -c '.data[0].embedding[:4]'
done
# identical vectors
```

On embed-gemma:300m, cosine(query, document) for the same text is 1.000000. It should differ, because the prefixes differ. With the task passed through it is 0.957706.

An unknown name (`"prompt_name":"not_a_task"`) or a non-string (`"prompt_name":7`) is also accepted, and the server answers 200 with a query embedding.

### Cause

The engine already supports every task. `embedding_task_type_t` has ten values ([`auto_embedding_model.hpp:33-44`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/include/AutoEmbeddingModel/auto_embedding_model.hpp#L33-L44)), and `Gemma_Embedding::_get_task_prefix` maps each one to its prefix ([`modeling_gemma_embedding.hpp:13-54`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/include/AutoEmbeddingModel/modeling_gemma_embedding.hpp#L13-L54)). The REST handler never reads the request's task and hardcodes `embedding_task_type_t::task_query` ([`rest_handler.cpp:900`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L900)).

### Expected

Read `prompt_name`, with `task_type` accepted as an alias, and pass the matching task to `embed()`. Refuse an unknown or non-string value with a 400 instead of embedding with a different task. A request with no task keeps today's `task_query` default.

### Fix we are carrying

https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/embed-task-prompt.patch

It maps the REST names (`query`/`search_query`, `document`/`search_document`, `clustering`, `classification`, `STS`, and so on) onto `embedding_task_type_t` and passes the result to `embed()`. It refuses unknown, non-string, or conflicting `prompt_name`/`task_type` values with 400 `invalid_value`. One resolved task applies to every element of an `input` array. The mapping and validation are ported from OpenFlowLM-Next's `SERVER-EMBED-TASK-PROMPT` (`openai_compat::task_names`/`resolve_task`/`task_policy`, Vegard Berget). The helpers need a `FASTFLOWLM_LINUX_LIMITED_MODELS` guard, as the patch shows. I can send this as a PR against `main` if that's useful.

Probe logs, before and after: https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/bench-logs/oflm-api-conformance-2026-09-28-after-174/README.md

### Environment

FLM v1.0.6 built from the tag, with our downstream request-handling patches, none of which touched this call before the fix. Model: embed-gemma:300m via `--embed 1`.
Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo), XDNA2 NPU, 8 columns. NixOS, Linux 7.2.8, amdxdna 0.10, NPU FW 1.1.2.65.

This is separate from the embedding-quality reports in #661, #647 and #732. It is about which prefix gets applied, not about the kernel output.

items.title: flm serve: streaming /api/chat segfaults the server on every request (insert() twice, generate() never called)
items.body:
### What happens

Every `POST /api/chat` with `"stream": true` crashes `flm serve` with SIGSEGV. The client gets no bytes back, and every other client loses the server too.

```bash
flm serve llama3.2:1b
curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:52625/api/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"llama3.2:1b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 5."}],"stream":true}'
# connection closes with no response; the flm process has exited (SIGSEGV)
```

It reproduces on llama3.2:1b and gemma4-it:e4b. The server log shows one `Prefill chunk 1/1` line, then nothing. Backtraces from the core dumps:

```
llama3.2:1b                                  gemma4-it:e4b
#0 Sampler::sample_greedy(buffer<bf16>&)     #0 Sampler::sample_greedy(buffer<bf16>&)
#1 AutoModel::_shared_insert(...)            #1 AutoModel::_shared_insert(...)
#2 Llama3::insert(...)                       #2 Gemma4e::insert(...)
#3 RestHandler::handle_chat(...)             #3 RestHandler::handle_chat(...)
```

### Cause

The streaming branch of `handle_chat` runs the `insert()` try block twice ([`rest_handler.cpp:792-819`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L792-L819)). It never calls `generate()` before `ostream.finalize_chat()` ([`:823`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L823)).

The first `insert()` writes the whole prompt to `token_history`. The second one then prefix-matches all of it in `AutoModel::_shared_insert` ([`automodel.cpp:184-201`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/common/AutoModel/automodel.cpp#L184-L201)). It erases every token, prefills an empty vector, and samples an empty logits buffer ([`:234`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/common/AutoModel/automodel.cpp#L234)).

This looks like the same code as #436, which reported empty chunks on v0.9.36 and was closed because the Ollama API is no longer maintained. On v1.0.6 the result is no longer an empty stream: the whole process crashes, including for clients that only use `/v1/*`. If the Ollama routes are staying unmaintained, removing `/api/chat` would also close this.

### Fix we are carrying

Replace the second `insert()` block with the `generate()` block that streaming `/api/generate` already uses ([`:690-697`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L690-L697)):
https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/stream-chat-generate.patch

The diff is small. Our copy of the file carries other patches, so the context lines differ from upstream's. With the fix, both models stream token chunks and then one `done: true` chunk with stats. The streamed text is byte-identical to the non-streaming reply, and there is one prefill per request. I can send this as a PR against `main` if that's useful.

Probes and logs: https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/bench-logs/oflm-api-conformance-2026-09-28-after-187/README.md

### Environment

FLM v1.0.6 built from the tag, with our downstream request-handling patches applied. In this block those patches change only the bodies of the `catch` clauses. The double `insert()` and the missing `generate()` are upstream code.
Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo), XDNA2 NPU, 8 columns. NixOS, Linux 7.2.8, amdxdna 0.10, NPU FW 1.1.2.65.

items.title: flm serve: a request body with invalid UTF-8 leaves the NPU locked, and every later request queues forever
items.body:
### What happens

One request whose body is not valid JSON and contains an invalid UTF-8 byte takes the NPU lock and never releases it. Every later request to an NPU route (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`) waits in the queue until the server is restarted.

```bash
flm serve llama3.2:1b
printf '{"messages": "\xe5"' | curl -s -m 10 http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @-
curl -s -m 60 http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"llama3.2:1b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say ok."}],"max_tokens":8}'
# the second request never completes
```

The server log shows `NPU Locked!` for the first request, then `invalid UTF-8 byte at index 174`, and never `NPU Lock Released!`.

### Expected

A 400 for the malformed body, and the lock released.

### Cause

1. `handle_request` tries to parse the body for logging ([`server.cpp:646-661`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L646-L661)). The parse fails, so `is_json` stays false, and `process_task` then skips its own guarded parse ([`:689-712`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L689-L712)).
2. The route lambda parses the body again with no guard ([`:1021-1023`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L1021-L1023)). The resulting `parse_error` lands in the catch at [`:782-797`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L782-L797).
3. That catch builds `{"error": "Handler exception: " + e.what()}` and calls `.dump()` ([`:787`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L787)). nlohmann quotes the offending bytes in `e.what()`, and the default `dump()` throws `type_error.316` on invalid UTF-8.
4. The second throw leaves the catch before `process_next_npu_request()` runs. It is caught only by the per-I/O-thread `try` around `ioc.run()` ([`:502-509`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L502-L509)), so the lock is never released.

We found a second path to the same leak by reading the source; we did not measure it. `request_id` is read into a `std::string` at [`server.cpp:719`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L719), outside every `try`, while the lock is held. A request with a non-string `request_id` (`"request_id": 5`) throws there and leaks the lock the same way. Also from reading the source: each such escape seems to end the `ioc.run()` loop of the I/O thread it happened on, so the thread pool shrinks by one per request.

### Fix we are carrying

https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/server-error-handling.patch

- `safe_dump()` dumps with `json::error_handler_t::replace`, so building the error body cannot throw. This is ported from OpenFlowLM-Next's `server.cpp` (Vegard Berget).
- A small RAII guard releases the NPU lock exactly once on every exit from `process_task`, including an exception nothing catches.
- A non-string `request_id` is refused with a 400 before it is read.
- A `json::parse_error` escaping a route lambda is answered with 400 "Invalid JSON".

With the patch, the request above gets a 400, and the log shows `NPU Locked!` and `NPU Lock Released!` around it. The next chat request completes.

### Environment

FLM v1.0.6 built from the tag, plus one downstream patch that only changes how `send_response` maps `error.code` to an HTTP status. That patch does not touch these paths.
Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo), XDNA2 NPU, 8 columns. NixOS, Linux 7.2.8, amdxdna 0.10, NPU FW 1.1.2.65. Model: llama3.2:1b.

We found this with `test_a_body_that_is_not_json_is_refused_and_the_server_keeps_serving` from OpenFlowLM-Next's server-api conformance suite.

items.title: flm serve crashes when a request is missing a required field (`POST {}`)
items.body:
### What happens

A request body that lacks a required field kills the `flm serve` process. No response is sent, and every later connection is refused until the server is restarted.

```bash
flm serve llama3.2:1b
curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:52625/api/show \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
# curl exit 56, HTTP 000; the flm process is gone
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1/models
# connection refused
```

We saw the same crash with `POST {}` on `/api/show`, `/api/generate` and `/v1/chat/completions`, each tested in isolation. `/api/chat` and `/v1/completions` read their required field the same way, but we did not isolate them.

The same pattern explains a milder symptom. When `/v1/embeddings` gets no `model`, the handler happens to survive, and it answers HTTP 200 with `{"error":"[json.exception.type_error.302] type must be string, but is invalid"}`. The value it read was garbage, not a missing-key error.

### Expected

A 400 naming the missing field, and the server keeps serving.

### Cause

The handlers take `const json& request` and read required fields with `operator[]`:

- `handle_show`: [`rest_handler.cpp:612`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L612) `request["model"]`
- `handle_generate`: [`:650`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L650) `request["prompt"]`
- `handle_chat`: [`:764`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L764) `request["messages"]`
- `handle_embeddings`: [`:882-889`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L882-L889) `request["model"]`, `request["input"]`
- `handle_openai_chat_completion`: [`:1103`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1103) `request["messages"]`
- `handle_openai_completion`: [`:1410`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/rest_handler.cpp#L1410) `request["prompt"]`

On a const `nlohmann::json`, `operator[]` with a missing key is undefined behaviour. It is guarded only by `JSON_ASSERT`, which a release build compiles out, so it does not throw, and the surrounding `try`/`catch` never runs. The handler dereferences the map's end iterator instead.

### Fix we are carrying

Check presence and type before each read, and refuse with a 400:
https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai/blob/46d7a73c1044435cec0ff08410e1a3bc87cbc544/pkgs/fastflowlm/patches/request-validation.patch

The `require_field()` helper is ported from OpenFlowLM-Next (`src/server/openai_compat.hpp`, Vegard Berget). Its error bodies carry an OpenAI-style string `code` (`"missing_required_parameter"`). Upstream `send_response` reads `error.code` with `.get<int>()` ([`server.cpp:736`](https://github.com/ROCm/FastFlowLM/blob/39ff855632431b642c1e4684121b97670c71a27b/src/server/server.cpp#L736)), which would throw on a string code. So the helper needs that line changed too. Our version of that change is in `server-error-handling.patch` in the same directory.

After the patch, all five endpoints answer `POST {}` with a 400 naming the field, and a normal chat request afterwards still completes. OpenFlowLM-Next's `specs/server-api/tests/test_request_validation.py` went from 0 of 22 passing to 14 passing with 8 skipped.

### Environment

FLM v1.0.6 built from the tag, plus one downstream patch that only changes how `send_response` maps `error.code` to an HTTP status. That patch does not touch these read paths.
Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo), XDNA2 NPU, 8 columns. NixOS, Linux 7.2.8, amdxdna 0.10, NPU FW 1.1.2.65. Model: llama3.2:1b.

We found this by running OpenFlowLM-Next's server-api conformance suite (`specs/server-api/tests/`, commit eb65600) against `flm serve`. Related but different trigger: #498.

items.title: chore: add security scanning workflows
items.body:
## Security Scanning Workflows Enablement

This PR adds standardized security scanning workflows and configurations from [`ROCm/rocm-repo-template`](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-repo-template).

### Security Controls
- PR Security Scan
- Weekly Security Scan
- Dependabot
- CodeQL, Bandit, Gitleaks, Trivy, and Zizmor

### Files added / updated
- `.github/workflows/pr-security-scan.yml` — scans every pull request
- `.github/workflows/weekly-security-scan.yml` — scheduled weekly scan
- `.github/dependabot.yml` — automated dependency updates
- `.github/scan_tools_configs/bandit.yml` — Python static analysis config
- `.github/scan_tools_configs/gitleaks.toml` — secret detection config
- `.github/scan_tools_configs/trivy.yml` — container/dependency vulnerability config
- `.github/scan_tools_configs/zizmor.yml` — GitHub Actions security config

### Why
This change aligns this repository with the ROCm GitHub Organization Security Baseline and enables consistent security controls across ROCm repositories.

items.title: [Bug][Linux] /v1/embeddings always fails with qds_device::wait() unexpected command state (Krackan Point, FLM 1.0.6)
items.body:
### Problem Description

On Linux, every request to `/v1/embeddings` fails with the same internal XRT error, deterministically, while chat completions on the same server instance keep working fine.

**Request:**
```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1/embeddings \
  -d '{"model":"embed-gemma:300m","input":"hola"}'
```

**Response (100% of requests):**
```json
{"error":"qds_device::wait() unexpected command state"}
```

Server log shows the request arriving and being accepted, then the error:
```
[LOG]  Target: /v1/embeddings
    "model": "embed-gemma:300m"
Embedding input[0]: hola
→ {"error":"qds_device::wait() unexpected command state"}
```

Notes:
- Happens with single-string input and with arrays.
- `flm serve llama3.2:1b --embed 1` loads both models successfully (`Embedding mode enabled: reserving additional 300MB`); failure only occurs at the actual embed dispatch.
- Without `--embed 1`, chat on the same box is fine (96 tok/s prefill / 42 tok/s decode with llama3.2:1b).
- The error message text matches the generic XRT/NPU queue-state error also seen in Xilinx/mlir-aie#1751 and amd/RyzenAI-SW#177.

Related issues (but not the same symptom): #732 and #661 report embeddings that complete but are wrong/collapsed on Linux; #647 reports non-determinism; #655 reports an IOCTL regression on the same chip family (Krackan Point). This report adds the case where the embed dispatch itself errors out on every request.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | AMD Ryzen AI 5 PRO 340 (Krackan Point), PCI `1022:17f0`, Lenovo subsystem |
| OS | Omarchy (Arch Linux), Wayland |
| Kernel | `7.2.5-4-omarchy` |
| NPU FW | 1.1.2.64 |
| Device | `/dev/accel/accel0` with 8 columns |
| amdxdna | in-tree, reported as `0.10` by `flm validate` |
| XRT | `xrt 2.21.75-14` + `xrt-plugin-amdxdna 2.21.75-2` (Arch `extra`) |
| FLM | `fastflowlm 1.0.6-1` (Arch `extra`) |
| Memlock | unlimited (via ulimit wrapper) |

`flm validate` output:
```
[Linux]  Kernel: 7.2.5-4-omarchy
[Linux]  NPU: /dev/accel/accel0 with 8 columns
[Linux]  NPU FW Version: 1.1.2.64
[Linux]  amdxdna version: 0.10
[Linux]  Memlock Limit: infinity
```

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
flm pull llama3.2:1b
flm pull embed-gemma:300m
flm serve llama3.2:1b --embed 1

curl http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-gemma:300m","input":"hola"}'
```

### Expected

A vector array response:
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[...],...}]}
```

### Actual

```json
{"error":"qds_device::wait() unexpected command state"}
```

CPU governor/pmode (`--pmode balanced`) does not change the outcome; also reproduced with `pmode` default. Model files pass `flm check` after a fresh verified download.

items.title: Qwen3.8 27b
items.body:
## Summary

Adds `qwen3-8mtp` — the Qwen3.8-27B engine — as a new model family, and adds the
runtime plumbing for **speculative decoding** driven by the model's MTP draft head.

Qwen3.8-27B is a hybrid stack: 64 decoder layers in the pattern
`[linear, linear, linear, full] x 16` (48 GatedDeltaNet + 16 full attention),
plus a 1-layer MTP head used as a draft model. The engine dispatches to the
NPU2 bitstreams checked in under `src/xclbins/Qwen3.8-27B-NPU2/`, with CPU
reference kernels as the fallback path.

Model is registered at `qwen3-8mtp:27b` → `FastFlowLM/Qwen3.8-27B-NPU2`
(Q4_K, 17.1 GB footprint, 4096 default context, 256 max prefill).

## What's in it

**New engine**
- `src/include/models/qwen3_8mtp/qwen3_8mtp_npu.hpp` + `src/lib/xrt/libqwen3_8mtp_npu.so`
- `src/common/AutoModel/modeling_qwen3_8mtp.cpp` — `AutoModel` wrapper
- `src/common/AutoModel/modeling_qwen3_8mtp_image.cpp` — vision tower host-side
  pipeline (active only when the checkpoint ships `vision_weight.q4nx`; images
  are rejected loudly on a text-only checkpoint rather than silently dropped)
- `src/test/qwen3_8mtp_npu/` — standalone driver for scoring the engine against
  a reference dump
- Registration in `all_models.hpp`, `automodel.hpp`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `model_list.json`

**Speculative decoding**
- Three new virtuals on `causal_lm`, all defaulted (not pure) so the other 16
  engines are unchanged in behaviour: `supports_speculation()`,
  `speculate(last_token, max_draft)`, `last_speculation_prime_us()`.
- `AutoModel::_shared_generate()` takes the speculative path only when the
  engine supports it **and** the sampler is truly greedy — `top_k == 1` and all
  three penalties neutral. Acceptance is an exact argmax compare, so running it
  under any other sampler would silently substitute greedy decoding for the
  user's configured sampler. The output would still be fluent, so nothing
  downstream would ever flag it; all four conditions are load-bearing.
- Per-token streaming, token history, EOS and length-limit handling are factored
  into a single `consume()` lambda shared by both paths, so the speculative
  branch cannot drift into emitting text past a stop token.
- The first speculative cycle after each prefill primes the draft head's KV
  cache over the prompt window. That is prefill-shaped work happening inside a
  `speculate()` call with the decode clock running, and it scales with prompt
  length — leaving it there makes decode tok/s a function of prompt size. The
  engine reports the split and the runtime moves it from `DECODING_TIME` to
  `PREFILL_TIME`.

**Profiling**
- `show_profile()` re-enables the sampling / token-encode / token-decode rows
  (previously commented out) and adds an **`Untimed`** remainder row.
  This was added because the gap was real and invisible: Qwen3.8's think
  preamble spent ~13 s of a 24 s run in four `forward()` calls that
  `_shared_generate()`'s `DECODING_TIME.reset()` then discarded.
  Caveat documented in-place: the narrow rows only compare against Total on a
  single-turn run, since `DECODING_TIME` resets per turn while `PREFILL_TIME`
  and `TOTAL_TIME` accumulate. A multi-turn session over-reports `Untimed`, and
  the row prints signed rather than clamping, so that case announces itself.
- `profiler::add_time(int64_t)` for transferring an already-measured interval
  between buckets (clamped at zero).

**minja**
- `is undefined` test. Upstream minja (3e4c61c) implements `is defined` but not
  its negation, and throws on the test *name* before looking at the value, so
  `x is undefined` fails even when `x` is set. Qwen3.8-27B's chat template opens
  with `{%- if enable_thinking is undefined or enable_thinking is true %}`.

## Blocking before merge: stale engine vtables

Adding virtuals to `causal_lm` is a **lockstep change**. Every engine `.so`
emits its own vtable and `flm` loads those prebuilt; appending to the base class
renumbers the vtable, so any `.so` not rebuilt keeps one that is short by the
added slots, and the first virtual call past the end segfaults — after a clean
prefill, with no diagnostic. A link check cannot catch this: the vtable symbol
still resolves, it is merely the wrong size.

This branch rebuilt only `libqwen3_8mtp_npu.so`. The other 16 are stale:

```
$ for f in src/lib/xrt/lib*_npu.so; do readelf -sW "$f" | grep -E '_ZTV.*_npu'; done
libqwen3_8mtp_npu.so   144  _ZTV14qwen3_8mtp_npu   <-- rebuilt
libqwen3_npu.so        120  _ZTV9qwen3_npu         <-- stale
libqwen3_6_moe_npu.so  120  _ZTV15qwen3_6_moe_npu  <-- stale
libgemma4_12b_npu.so   120  _ZTV14gemma4_12b_npu   <-- stale
... (13 more, all 120)
```

All engine `.so` files under `src/lib/xrt/` need to be regenerated and re-copied
in this PR before it is safe to merge — otherwise every model except
Qwen3.8-27B crashes on its first decode step. Verify with the `readelf` command
above rather than with "it compiled" or "it linked".

(Note: the ABI comment in `causal_lm.hpp` says the change takes the vtable from
120 to 136 bytes — it is 144, since three virtuals were added, not two. Worth
correcting so the number in the comment matches what `readelf` prints.)

## Also needs a look before merge

- **`prompt.txt`** at the repo root looks like a stray scratch file (an LLM
  prompt about dispatch-count profiling) rather than something intended to ship.
  Probably wants deleting.
- **`.claude/` in `.gitignore`** — fine if the project wants it, flagging only
  because it is unrelated to the model.

## Testing

- `src/test/qwen3_8mtp_npu/` driver runs a text turn and (with `-i`) one
  multimodal turn, scoring intermediates against a reference dump.
- Speculation statistics are exposed engine-side (`mean_accepted_length()`,
  `draft_hit_rate()`, `speculation_cycles()`, `speculation_timing()`,
  `speculation_phase_fraction()`) because a broken draft path is otherwise
  **silent** — verify overrides every rejected draft with the base model's own
  argmax, so bad drafting still produces correct text and merely burns time.
  `speculation_phase_fraction()` is deliberately normalised by measured cycle
  time, not by the sum of the parts, so a double-counted phase pushes it above
  1.0 instead of hiding itself.

Still to confirm on hardware:
- [ ] All 16 other engines rebuilt; `readelf` vtable sizes agree
- [ ] Non-speculative models unchanged (regression run on qwen3, gemma4)
- [ ] Draft hit rate / accepted-length on a representative prompt set
- [ ] `Untimed` row sanity-checked on a single-turn run

items.title: Tool calling serializes boolean arguments as strings with Qwen3.5 ("True" instead of true)
items.body:
Description

FastFlowLM v1.0.6 serializes a tool argument defined as JSON Schema
boolean as a JSON string when using qwen3.5:9b.

The tool schema explicitly defines:

"accepted": {
  "type": "boolean"
}

However, FastFlowLM returns:

{"accepted":"True"}

instead of:

{"accepted":true}

This causes OpenAI-compatible clients that validate tool arguments
against the supplied JSON Schema to reject the tool call.

Environment

FastFlowLM: v1.0.6

Model: qwen3.5:9b

Linux portable build: fastflowlm_1.0.6_linux.tar.gz

API: /v1/chat/completions

Minimal reproducer

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen3.5:9b","stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Call confirm_result with accepted set to true."}],"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"confirm_result","description":"Confirm the result","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"accepted":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["accepted"]}}}],"tool_choice":{"type":"function","function":{"name":"confirm_result"}}}'

Actual result

FastFlowLM returns the tool arguments as:

"arguments":"{\"accepted\":\"True\"}"

Decoded:

{
  "accepted": "True"
}

The value is a JSON string.

Expected result

The tool arguments should preserve the type specified by the JSON
Schema:

"arguments":"{\"accepted\":true}"

Decoded:

{
  "accepted": true
}

The value should be a JSON boolean.

Additional information

The model's raw tool output contains:

<parameter=accepted>
True
</parameter>

FastFlowLM then converts this to:

{"accepted":"True"}

So it appears that the tool-call argument conversion/serialization step
does not coerce the generated value according to the parameter type
declared in the supplied tool JSON Schema.

This is reproducible with a minimal request and does not require a large
context or a multi-turn conversation.

items.title: flm serve OpenAI-compatible endpoint hardcodes max_tokens default = 4096 → long responses are silently truncated (finish_reason: "length") when the client omits max_tokens
items.body:
### Title
`flm serve` OpenAI-compatible endpoint hardcodes `max_tokens` default = 4096 → long responses are silently truncated (`finish_reason: "length"`) when the client omits `max_tokens`

### Environment
- FLM version: 1.0.6 (Linux package `fastflowlm 1.0.6-1`, Arch Linux, x86_64)
- Hardware: AMD Ryzen™ AI NPU (XDNA2, NPU2 kernels)
- Model: `qwen3.5:9b` (Qwen3.5-9B-NPU2), server started with `--ctx-len 64000 --pmode turbo`
- Client: OpenAI-compatible (opencode 2.0.12) + direct curl

### Summary
The `/v1/chat/completions` handler falls back to a hardcoded `max_tokens = 4096` when the request body does not include `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens`:

```cpp
request.value("max_tokens", 4096)   // rest_handler.cpp, three request sites (~lines 655 / 1106 / 1420 in 1.0.6)
```

Several common OpenAI-compatible clients never send `max_tokens` (verified: opencode 2.0.12 sends only `model`/`store`/`stream`/`stream_options`). For those clients this 4096 cap becomes an invisible hard ceiling: any generation longer than 4096 tokens is cut mid-sentence with `finish_reason: "length"`, even when the model would have stopped naturally. This truncates long outputs (webpages, code files) with no way for the client to detect the cause other than parsing `finish_reason`.

### Reproduction
1. Start: `flm serve qwen3.5:9b --ctx-len 64000 -p 52626`
2. POST without `max_tokens`:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52626/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen3.5:9b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Build a complete single-file HTML page with embedded JS (form, validation, dark mode)..."}]}'
```

Observed: `"finish_reason":"length"`, `"completion_tokens":4096`, output cut mid-JS (at `<section id="contact`), never reaching `</html>`.

3. Same message WITH `"max_tokens":12000`: `"finish_reason":"stop"`, completed `</html>`, `"completion_tokens":3772`.

### Evidence (same model, same server)

| Request | max_tokens | finish_reason | completion_tokens | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | (absent) | length | 4096 | Truncated mid-JS |
| B | 12000 | stop | 3772 | Completed `</html>` |
| C | 12000 (+ `think:true`, `reasoning_effort:"medium"`) | stop | 4940 | Completed |

Decode speed ≈ 9.2 tok/s → each truncated run wastes ~7 minutes of NPU time while producing a broken response.

### Expected behavior
Following the OpenAI convention (and Ollama's), when the client omits the output budget, generation should be bounded only by the context window — not by a fixed 4096 ceiling. If a default is kept, it should be derived from the active context, e.g. `min(16384, MAX_L - prompt_tokens)`, and ideally configurable (`--max-tokens` env/flag, or per-model default from `model_list.json`'s `default_context_length`).

### Related observations (same session, feel free to split)
1. Default sampler for Qwen3.5 in 1.0.6: `presence_penalty 1.5`, `frequency_penalty 1.0`, `temperature 0.7`, `top_p 0.8`. The aggressive penalties visibly degrade long code generation; opencode also does not forward client-provided sampling options, so these defaults apply in practice.
2. With `"think": true` + `"reasoning_effort"`, FLM produced ~4.4K chars of reasoning but never emitted the response marker: reasoning was appended to `content` while `reasoning_content` stayed empty.

### Suggested fix
In `src/server/rest_handler.cpp`, replace the three hardcoded defaults:

```cpp
// before
request.value("max_tokens", 4096)

// after
request.value("max_tokens", std::min(16384, max_len - prompt_len))
```

Happy to open a PR if this behavior is confirmed as unintentional.

items.title: feat(rai): run Phi-4, Qwen3, Gemma 4, and Qwen3.5 Q8_0 GGUFs through ryzenai-corelib
items.body:
Adds a `rai` backend that runs Q8_0 GGUFs on `aie_next` NPUs through AMD's `ryzenai-corelib` 0.11.0, next to the existing FastFlowLM NPU2 path.

## Models

Each model is its own catalog tag with `supported_platforms: ["aie_next"]`, beside the NPU2 entry for the same family. A tag ending in `-rai` runs on corelib; every other tag keeps running on FastFlowLM's own kernels.

| Tag | Model |
|---|---|
| `phi4-mini-it-rai:4b` | Phi-4-mini-instruct Q8_0 |
| `qwen3-rai:0.6b` `qwen3-rai:1.7b` `qwen3-rai:4b` `qwen3-rai:8b` | Qwen3 dense |
| `gemma4-it-rai:e2b` `gemma4-it-rai:e4b` | Gemma 4 E2B / E4B, text only |
| `qwen3.5-rai:9b` | Qwen3.5-9B Q8_0 |

## What the PR adds

- **Engines** for Phi-4, Qwen3, Gemma 4 and Qwen3.5 under `models/<family>/rai/aie_next/`. Weights are read straight from the GGUF; each one is a single `*_weights_create` call with role-tagged sources, and packed weights are cached next to the model for the next load.
- **Shared rai code** under `src/common/rai` and `src/include/rai`: the corelib loader (static on Windows, `dlopen` on Linux), GGUF mapping, host ops, the weight cache, and the kernel grid that sizes every buffer from the kernels corelib reports.
- **Backend registry.** Every family registers its engine through one registry, so the frontends load models the same way on either backend. The FastFlowLM engines' headers move to `models/<family>/flm/aie2p/`.
- **Catalog.** Entries name the NPU generation they run on, and the catalog drops entries this build or this machine cannot run.
- **One NPU device per process.** FastFlowLM uses the device behind corelib's hardware context instead of opening a second one.
- **Frontend fixes these models need.** `LM_Config` reads `vocab_size` from `text_config` when the top level has none (Gemma 4 and Qwen3.5). The server refuses a model name the catalog does not have before resolving it.

Requirements: `-DFLM_ENABLE_RAI=ON`, corelib 0.11.0 headers from after the one-`*_weights_create`-per-operator API, and an `aie_next` NPU. Usable context is 4095 tokens. A missing or wrong-version corelib fails the load instead of falling back to CPU or NPU2. Packaging and CI for the rai path are not part of this PR.

## Results

**Unit tests** (`src/test/phi4_rai`, `src/test/qwen3_rai`, `src/test/gemma4_rai`, Windows): Phi-4 9/9, Qwen3 1/1, Gemma 4 10/10. The three that need real hardware or real model files — `test_real_corelib`, `test_gemma4_real_gguf`, `test_gemma4_tokenizer` — pass on an `aie_next` machine.

**End to end** on an `aie_next` NPU with `flm serve <tag> --ctx-len 4096`: each model got `/api/generate` with prompts of exactly 64, 256, 1024 and 2048 tokens and up to 8 new tokens. All 20 requests returned coherent text, both when packing weights and when loading them from the cache.

| Tag | Prefill at 64 / 256 / 1024 / 2048 tokens | Load: packing / from cache |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen3-rai:0.6b` | 0.18 / 0.06 / 0.26 / 0.42 s | 3.0 s / 0.7 s |
| `phi4-mini-it-rai:4b` | 0.16 / 0.12 / 0.62 / 1.59 s | 1.0 s / 1.2 s |
| `gemma4-it-rai:e2b` | 0.38 / 0.21 / 0.70 / 1.14 s | 5.8 s / 1.8 s |
| `gemma4-it-rai:e4b` | 0.29 / 0.29 / 1.13 / 1.86 s | 11.1 s / 2.0 s |
| `qwen3.5-rai:9b` | 4.9 / 16.4 / 64.5 / 129.0 s | 29.7 s (not cached) |

`qwen3-rai:1.7b`, `4b` and `8b` were not run.

items.title: [Bug, Issue]: ASR model (whisper-large-v3-turbo) not explicitly named in v1/models, so doesn't work with stricter openAI compatible connections
items.body:
### Problem Description

This is an issue related to the running the whisper model with strict open AI compatible connection.
When running FastFlowLM with the ASR pipeline enabled (flm serve --asr 1), the /v1/models endpoint only broadcasts text and vision models. It fails to list the active Whisper/ASR model in the payload.

This creates a routing conflict with strict OpenAI-compatible clients (like TypeWhisper) that rely on /v1/models to populate their UI dropdowns. Because the ASR model is missing, users are forced to select another model. FastFlowLM then receives the audio payload, locks the NPU, attempts to process the audio through the text model, and returns an empty transcription string without throwing an error.

### Operating System

Windows 11 10.0.26200

### CPU

AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 w/ Radeon 890M

### GPU

XDNA 2 NPU, 50 TOPS (AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370)

### ROCm Version

Ryzen AI NPU (Driver Version: 32.0.203.311)

### Installation Method

Other (describe in Additional Information)

### Installed ROCm Packages / Versions

<details>
<summary>Installed ROCm packages / versions</summary>

```
N/A - Running on Windows 11 with Ryzen AI NPU. 
No traditional ROCm packages are installed.

- FastFlowLM: Installed via the Windows flm-setup.msi
- AMD NPU Driver: [ 32.0.203.311]
```

</details>


### ROCm Component

_No response_

### Steps to Reproduce


Launch FastFlowLM on Windows with the ASR pipeline enabled by running flm serve --asr 1 (default port 52625).

Query the /v1/models endpoint. Observe that only text/vision models (e.g., gemma4-it:12b) are returned in the JSON payload, while the active ASR model is missing.

Open an OpenAI-compatible client (e.g., TypeWhisper) and point its API base URL to [http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1](http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1).

Attempt to configure the transcription model. Because the ASR model is not broadcast, select an available model from the UI dropdown. It does not allow for typing an arbitrary model in or leaving blank as it is strict.

Initiate a voice dictation. The client sends a POST request with audio data to /v1/audio/transcriptions targeting the selected model.

Check the FastFlowLM terminal logs. Observe that the NPU locks, processes the payload, and releases without throwing an error.

Observe the client UI of typewhisper, which receives an empty transcription string (rather than an API error) and outputs "No speech detected."

### (Optional for Linux users) Output of rocminfo --support

<details>
<summary>rocminfo --support output</summary>

```
Paste output here
```

</details>


### Additional Information

I used FastflowLM directly so I don't have details on ROCM installation/version.
